section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: True or false: designing and building a business app from a blank page in Power Apps, without writing code in a traditional programming language, is what's called a Canvas App.
explanation: Canvas Apps in Power Apps Definition Canvas apps allow you to design and build business applications from a blank canvas in Microsoft Power Apps. They do not require traditional programming languages. The app is designed by dragging and dropping elements onto the canvas, giving complete control over the layout. Key Characteristics Drag-and-drop interface makes them easier for non-technical users to create. Highly flexible and customizable to meet specific business needs. Not based on a pre-defined data model, which can make maintenance and troubleshooting more complex. Comparison with Model-driven Apps Canvas Apps: Flexible, user-driven design, ideal for custom layouts and specific scenarios. Model-driven Apps: Built on a structured data model, easier to maintain and scale, but require knowledge of data modeling. Example Scenarios Sales team: Use a canvas app to create a lead management app for tracking leads, managing opportunities, and closing deals. Marketing team: Use a model-driven app to build a CRM solution that manages customer data, sales pipelines, and marketing communications. Use Cases of Canvas Apps Project dashboards: Display key metrics, timelines, milestones, and resource allocation. Task management: Track and update tasks, priorities, and completion dates. Collaboration and communication: Enable discussion boards, chat, and notifications. Resource management: Assign team members based on availability and skills. Time tracking: Log hours spent on tasks for billing and reporting. Expense tracking: Record and submit project-related expenses. Risk and issue management: Log risks, assign owners, and track mitigation. Document repository: Store and organize contracts, deliverables, and project files. Approval workflows: Streamline approvals for changes or budgets. Project status reporting: Generate real-time dashboards and reports. Vendor and supplier collaboration: Coordinate procurement and delivery schedules. Feedback and surveys: Collect input from stakeholders and clients for continuous improvement. Exam Tips Expect scenario-based questions distinguishing canvas apps from model-driven apps.

text: How can data sources actually be used together with Power Apps canvas apps?

explanation: Multiple Data Sources in Power Apps Key Points to Remember Power Apps allows you to build comprehensive and dynamic apps that pull data from multiple sources. Supported sources include cloud services, databases, SharePoint, Excel, APIs, and more. This flexibility enhances app functionality by enabling interaction with diverse datasets. Power Apps supports over 300 prebuilt connectors and also allows you to build custom connectors if needed. Connections can be made to both cloud-based and on-premises data sources. How to Access Multiple Data Sources Open the Data Sources pane in the Power Apps Designer. Create a connection to each required data source. Once connected, you can use data from those sources directly in your app. Advantages of Using Multiple Data Sources Combine data: Merge information from different systems (e.g., CRM + database) into a single view. Enrich data: Add context by combining sources (e.g., social media + CRM for deeper customer insights). section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: In Power Apps, if a team member needs to view and use an app but must not be able to change it, which permission level should you give them?
explanation: The correct answer is Users. Users must be explicitly assigned the 'User' permission in Power Apps; it is not automatically granted. These roles are different from those assigned at the environmental levels. (Environment Admin & Environment Maker role). Let's explore the capabilities and use cases of the Owner, Co-owner, and User roles in the Power Platform: Owner: Capabilities: Owners have full control over the resources within an environment, including apps, data, solutions, and settings. They can create, modify, and delete apps, data tables, connectors, and solutions. Owners can manage user access, sharing, and permissions for all resources. They have the authority to manage and configure environment settings, including security and data sources. Use Case: Owners are typically administrators or technical leads responsible for the overall management of projects or teams within an environment. They create and oversee the setup of environments, manage permissions, and ensure the proper functioning of apps and data. Co-owner: Capabilities: Co-owners share many of the same capabilities as Owners, such as creating, editing, and sharing apps and solutions. However, they cannot delete the environment itself or change its owner. Use Case: Co-owners are individuals who collaborate closely with Owners, assisting in the development and management of apps, solutions, and data tables. They play a key role in app development and maintenance without having the authority to make environment-level changes. User: Capabilities: Users with the User role can view and use the apps that are shared with them. They can interact with the app's functionality, enter data, and access information, but they cannot modify the app itself. Users can access and interact with apps but cannot modify configurations, solutions, or environments. Use Case: Users include employees, customers, partners, or stakeholders who need to access and utilize apps for specific tasks or information retrieval. This role ensures that those who require access to apps can use them without the risk of unintended changes. Summary: Owner: Full control over all resources, including creation, modification, and settings. Responsible for environment management. Co-owner: Similar capabilities to Owners, except cannot delete the environment or change its owner. Collaborates in app development and management. User: Limited to using shared apps, interacting with functionality, and accessing information without altering the app's design. Assigning roles appropriately ensures a well-organized and secure environment within the Power Platform, allowing users to collaborate effectively while maintaining control over data and app development. Exam Tips: Expect questions distinguishing between Owner, Co-Owner, and User roles. Understanding how permissions are assigned in Power Apps will help you answer confidently.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Your sales team badly needs a mobile app that shows rows from a SharePoint list, where each record needs to display several pieces of information at once. Which Power Apps tool would you reach for to build this?

options.text: Create a gallery to display the sales rows.
Create an input control to display the sales rows.
Create a form to display the sales rows

explanation: Gallery Control in Power Apps Correct Answer Create a gallery to display the sales rows. Explanation The Gallery control is designed to display tables of data from a data source such as SharePoint, Excel, or Dataverse. It provides a dynamic list or grid-like view of records, allowing you to show multiple pieces of information about each row. Galleries are highly customizable: you can include text, images, numbers, and other fields. For editing individual records, a Form control can be used alongside the Gallery. Features of Gallery Control Dynamic Data Display: Automatically shows records from a connected data source. Customizable Layout: Arrange fields, images, buttons, and controls within each item. Data Binding: Connects directly to SharePoint, Excel, Dataverse, or other sources. Multiple Data Fields: Display comprehensive information for each record. Interaction: Configure actions when users click or tap on items. Scrolling: Suitable for large datasets, allowing users to scroll through records. Sorting and Filtering: Implement options to refine and search records dynamically. Use Cases of Gallery Control Displaying Data Lists: Contacts, products, tasks, or records from databases. Detail Views: Navigate to detailed screens when an item is selected. Photo Albums and Image Galleries: Scrollable image collections with detail views. Newsfeeds and Updates: Chronological lists of posts or activity logs. Task Lists and Checklists: Track tasks and mark them as complete. Catalogues and Product Listings: Showcase items for e-commerce or browsing. Surveys and Questionnaires: Display questions and options for user responses. Directory and Contact Lists: Show contact details like name, email, and phone. Dynamic Filtering and Searching: Allow users to find records quickly. User Profiles: Display and navigate through user profile information. Custom Navigation: Create menus or buttons for app navigation. Interactive Dashboards: Combine with other controls for rich, interactive views. Exam Tips Galleries are central to Canvas Apps for displaying multiple records.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: You're building a Power App that scans barcodes and shows the scanned item's info on screen. Which control category does the barcode scanner fall under?
explanation: Barcode Scanner Control in Power Apps Correct Control For creating a Power App that can scan barcodes and display the scanned item’s information, you would use the Barcode scanner control from the Media controls category. How It Works The Barcode scanner control interacts with the device’s camera to capture barcode data. Once scanned, the barcode information can be passed into the app. Other controls (like galleries or forms) can then be used to display or edit the scanned item’s details. Types of Controls in Power Apps Gallery Displays lists of data items (e.g., products, contacts, tasks). Not designed for capturing input like barcode scanning. Useful for showing scanned item information after capture. Media Controls Designed to capture or display media such as images, audio, video, and barcodes. The Barcode scanner control is part of this category. Enables scanning of various barcode types and integrates with app logic to process results. Forms Used for data entry and editing. Includes input fields like text boxes, drop-downs, and buttons. A barcode scanner can feed data into a form, but forms themselves are not designed for media capture. Example Workflow User scans a product barcode using the Barcode scanner control. The scanned data is passed into the app. A Gallery control displays product details (name, price, stock). A Form control allows editing or updating product information. Exam Tips Barcode scanner = Media control. Galleries = display lists of records. Forms = data entry and editing. Expect scenario-based questions where you must identify the correct control for scanning, displaying, or editing data. References: Audio and Video Controls in Power Apps - Power Apps | Microsoft Learn Recommended Youtube Videos: Power Apps Gallery Design Ideas - YouTube

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A company is building a personal-finance mobile app (budgeting, expense tracking, investments) where users should only be able to do what's relevant to their role. Which Dataverse feature groups privileges and controls access to app features and data like this?

Security Role - Security roles and privileges - Power Platform | Microsoft Learn Definition: A security role refers to a predefined set of permissions and access rights granted to users or groups within an organization's information system. It determines what actions and resources a user or group can access. Use: Security roles are primarily used to manage and enforce the principle of least privilege, ensuring that users only have the permissions necessary for their job functions. This helps enhance security by limiting unauthorized access and reducing the potential for data breaches or misuse of resources. Types: Different roles can have varying levels of access, such as read-only, read-write, or administrative privileges.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: As a security admin for a Power Platform-using company, you need a role for users who create new resources, apps, connections, APIs, gateways, flows, but shouldn't have access to environment data. Which role fits?

Their role is focused on building and distributing apps, not on managing or securing the environment itself. Why Other Options Are Incorrect System Administrator Role: Grants full administrative control over the environment. Can add or remove users or groups from Environment Admin or Environment Maker roles. Can provision a Dataverse database for the environment. Can view and manage all resources created within the environment. Can set data loss prevention policies. Can manage environment settings. Exam Tips Environment Maker = build and share apps/resources, but no direct access to environment data. System Administrator = full control, including user management, Dataverse provisioning, and environment policies. Expect scenario-based questions distinguishing between Environment Maker and System Administrator roles. text: You're assigning roles and permissions in a system, and need one where users can configure things but don't get full access to all environment data unless it's explicitly granted. Which role is this?

Typical tasks include: Designing forms, views, and dashboards Creating and managing business rules Configuring tables, columns, relationships, and app components Customizing model-driven apps to align with business requirements Permissions A System Customizer: Can modify the user interface and user experience Can customize Dataverse components within a specific environment Can create and modify app components such as forms, views, charts, and business rules Primarily focuses on application customization rather than environment administration Data Access A System Customizer does not automatically have full access to all business data in Dataverse Data access depends on the security privileges assigned to the role Additional access may need to be explicitly granted Environment Maker The Environment Maker role is responsible for creating resources in an environment. Capabilities include: Building apps, flows, chatbots, and connections Creating custom connectors and gateways Sharing apps with users or groups Important limitation: Environment Makers do not automatically have access to Dataverse data Focus: Resource creation and app building, not advanced customization or governance System Administrator The System Administrator role has full administrative control over the environment. Capabilities include: Managing users and security roles Configuring environment settings Managing Dataverse databases Viewing and managing all data and resources Setting Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies Focus: Administration, governance, and security management

User: Capabilities: Users with the User role can view and use the apps that are shared with them. section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: As a team lead responsible for sharing an important model-driven app with teammates and stakeholders, which statement accurately describes how that sharing process works?

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: In model-driven apps, how do rows and columns in a table relate to each other?

options.text: A. Rows represent individual entities, and columns store attributes of those entities
B. Rows store attributes, and columns represent individual entities
C. Rows and columns are used to navigate between work areas
D. Rows and columns are only used in the service app

explanation: Rows represent individual entities (e.g., a person in the Contact table), and columns store attributes (e.g., first name, family name, email address) of those entities. Why the other options are incorrect: B. Rows store attributes, and columns represent individual entities This reverses the actual relationship. Rows are the entities (e.g., each person), and columns are the attributes (e.g., name, email). So this statement is factually incorrect. C. Rows and columns are used to navigate between work areas Navigation between work areas is done using the work-area menu, not rows and columns. Rows and columns are for data storage and structure, not navigation. D. Rows and columns are only used in the service app Rows and columns are used in all apps that include tables, not just the service app. Tables like Contact and Account appear in multiple apps and areas, making this statement false.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Which of these is a key difference between canvas apps and model-driven apps when it comes to app design considerations?

options.text: A. Canvas apps are Dataverse-driven, while Model-driven apps are not Dataverse-driven
B. Canvas apps focus on tasks or screens, while Model-driven apps focus on back-office processes
C. Canvas apps have responsive and consistent UI, while Model-driven apps have custom UI
D. Canvas apps are designed for data relationship navigation, while Model-driven apps focus on user personalization

explanation: Canvas Apps vs Model-driven Apps 1. Purpose and Focus Canvas Apps Task-focused or screen-focused. Designed for specific user interactions and tailored experiences. Best for apps where the user interface (UI) needs to be highly customized. Model-driven Apps Process-focused or back-office-focused. Designed for managing workflows and business processes. Best for apps where data relationships and structured navigation are critical. 2. Data Source Canvas Apps Can connect to Dataverse or non-Dataverse sources (e.g., SharePoint, SQL, Excel, APIs). Flexible in integrating multiple connectors. Model-driven Apps Always Dataverse-driven. Relies on Dataverse tables, relationships, and metadata to define app structure. 3. User Interface (UI) Canvas Apps Custom UI: developers design the layout using drag-and-drop. Offers pixel-perfect control over placement, colors, and branding. Ideal for apps requiring personalization and embedding into other solutions. Model-driven Apps Responsive and consistent UI generated automatically. Standardized layouts across devices (desktop, tablet, mobile). Prioritizes usability and consistency over customization. 4. Navigation and Data Relationships Canvas Apps Focus on user personalization and embedding into specific workflows. Navigation is flexible and defined by the app maker. Model-driven Apps Designed for data relationship navigation. Automatically generates forms, views, and dashboards based on Dataverse schema. Ideal for scenarios where users need to move between related records. 5. Common Use Cases Canvas Apps Field service apps. Employee self-service portals. Custom dashboards. Mobile-first apps with tailored UI. Model-driven Apps Customer relationship management (CRM). Case management systems. Project tracking and resource allocation. Compliance and audit workflows. 6. Exam Pitfalls (Incorrect Options Explained) A is incorrect: Canvas apps can be Dataverse or non-Dataverse-driven, while Model-driven apps are always Dataverse-driven. C is incorrect: Canvas apps have custom UI, while Model-driven apps have responsive and consistent UI. D is incorrect: Model-driven apps are designed for data relationship navigation, while Canvas apps focus on user personalization and embedding. Exam Tip Canvas apps = flexibility, personalization, multiple data sources. Model-driven apps = structure, consistency, Dataverse-only, process-driven. Expect scenario-based questions where you must choose the right app type for a business need. References: Describe the differences between canvas apps and model-driven apps - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: What's a major benefit of using canvas apps in Power Apps?

options.text: A. They are limited to data stored in Microsoft Dataverse.
B. They enable designers to build apps using drag-and-drop controls and familiar formulas.
C. They demand expert-level programming knowledge for development and deployment

explanation: Canvas apps offer a flexible design experience where users can visually arrange elements and use Excel-style expressions to define logic. A is incorrect because Canvas apps can connect to a wide range of data sources, not just Dataverse. C is incorrect because Canvas apps are designed for low-code/no-code development, making them accessible to non-developers.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Which of these scenarios is the best example of when you'd use a model-driven app?

options.text: A. Designing a custom app with drag-and-drop controls to track employee attendance using a non-Dataverse data source.
B. Creating a responsive app for managing complex business processes with built-in data relationship navigation.
C. Building a task-focused app with a personalized user interface for embedding into a website.
D. Developing a screen-focused app that uses Excel-like expressions for logic and calculations.

explanation: Model-driven apps are ideal for managing complex business processes, leveraging Dataverse as the data source, and providing built-in navigation for data relationships. A is incorrect because Model-driven apps are Dataverse-driven and do not use drag-and-drop controls for design. C is incorrect because personalized UI and embedding are characteristics of Canvas apps. D is incorrect because Excel-like expressions are used in Canvas apps, not Model-driven apps.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: After you've finished designing a model-driven app, what's the crucial step to make sure users can actually get to it?

options.text: A. Save and publish the app
B. Assign appropriate security roles to users
C. Include relevant tables in the app

explanation: Saving and Publishing Apps Final Step in Deployment Saving and publishing the app is the critical final step that makes it accessible to users. If the app is only saved but not published, it remains in draft mode and cannot be used by others. Publishing ensures the app is live and available in the environment. Why Other Options Are Wrong B: Controlling access and permissions is important for security, but it does not make the app visible. Even with correct permissions, the app must be published before users can access it. C: Designing the app is part of the creation process. This involves building forms, adding logic, and customizing the UI. However, design alone does not deploy the app. Publishing is required to move from design to usage. Exam Tip For PL-900, clearly distinguish between design, security, and deployment steps. Design = building and customizing the app. Security = assigning roles and permissions. Deployment = publishing the app so it becomes live and usable. Publishing is the step that transitions the app from draft to production use.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: A real estate company needs an app for field agents to capture property details, take photos, and schedule open houses. Which type of app suits this best?

options.text: C. Both canvas and model-driven apps

explanation: Canvas apps are ideal for scenarios requiring a highly customized user interface and integration with device capabilities, such as capturing photos and scheduling tasks. B is incorrect because Model-driven apps are better suited for managing structured business processes and data relationships, not for task-focused, UI-intensive needs. C is incorrect because this scenario specifically benefits from the flexibility and device integration offered by Canvas apps. Exam Tips: For scenario-based questions, focus on the purpose of the app, the type of user, and the required functionality: If the app needs custom UI, device integration (camera, GPS), or is task/screen-focused, it's likely a Canvas app. If the app is process-driven, uses Dataverse, and needs standardized UI with data relationships, it's likely a Model-driven app. Read carefully for clues like “custom interface,” “field agents,” or “device features”, these often point to Canvas apps. Practice matching real-world use cases to app types. Microsoft loves testing your ability to apply concepts to business scenarios.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: When you manually trigger a flow, what options are actually available to you?
explanation: How They Work in Power Automate These inputs are added to the Power Apps interface. When a user triggers a button in Power Apps, the flow collects the input values and uses them in actions within Power Automate. Example: A user enters their name (Text Input), selects a date (Date Input), and uploads a file (File Input). The flow can then send an email with the name, schedule a task for the date, and attach the file. When creating a Power Automate flow using Power Apps, you can include various types of input fields to collect information from users when they initiate the flow. Some common types of input fields that you can use: Text Input: Users can enter text or characters. This is useful for capturing names, descriptions, comments, and other textual information. Number Input: Users can enter numerical values. This can be used for quantities, amounts, IDs, and other numeric data. Email Input: Users can provide email addresses. This is valuable for sending notifications or emails as part of the flow. Date and Time Input: Users can select dates and times from a calendar or input them manually. Useful for capturing specific dates, deadlines, or scheduling information. File Input: Users can upload files. Useful for collecting documents, images, or any type of files as input. Boolean (Yes/No) Input: Users can indicate a true or false value, often represented as a checkbox. This is suitable for simple yes/no or on/off decisions. These input fields can be added to the Power Apps interface when configuring a button trigger that initiates a Power Automate flow. Reference Sites: Six types of user inputs - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Which type of flow lets you use Robotic Process Automation?
explanation: Robotic Process Automation (RPA) in Power Automate is specifically supported through Desktop flows. These flows are designed to automate tasks on your computer by mimicking human interactions with software, like clicking buttons, entering data, or extracting information. Desktop flows are built using Power Automate Desktop, and they can also be triggered from cloud flows to create hybrid automation, where cloud flows handle scalable backend logic and desktop flows manage local app automation. Use cases of Desktop Flow: 1. Invoice Processing Automation Extract data from scanned invoices using OCR and auto-populate fields in accounting software, cutting down manual entry time dramatically. 2. Legacy Application Integration Automate interactions (clicks, keystrokes) with outdated systems that don’t support modern APIs, keeping workflows smooth without costly updates. 3. Data Extraction Scrape information from a website and save it to Excel, ideal for financial data, product listings, or market research. 4. IT Helpdesk Automation Automatically reset passwords by accessing local management tools and logging results into a ticketing system like ServiceNow. 5. Automated Report Distribution Pull data from emails and Excel, compile it into a formatted report, and email it to managers at scheduled intervals.

text: A company's agent answers questions correctly but can't actually perform any actions. What best explains why?

options.text: A. The agent has no channels configured.

explanation: Agents in Power Platform (Copilot Studio) can do two broad things: Answer questions - using topics, knowledge bases, or natural language understanding. Perform actions - by connecting to external systems or services through tools (such as Power Automate flows, Dataverse operations, or APIs). In this scenario, the agent is able to answer questions correctly, which means it has topics or knowledge configured. However, it cannot perform business actions like creating records, sending emails, or triggering workflows. The reason is that tools are not configured. section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Which of these are valid ways an approver can respond to an approval request in Power Automate? (Select all that apply)
explanation: Responding via Outlook Once an approval request is triggered, approvers receive a detailed email notification outlining all the relevant information about the request. From this email, they can: Review the request to understand its context and requirements. Approve or reject the request instantly by clicking the appropriate button embedded in the email. Add comments to share other insights, feedback, or context regarding their decision. This approach is convenient for individuals who rely heavily on their email inbox for daily tasks, allowing them to handle approvals without switching platforms. Responding in Microsoft Teams For organizations that use Microsoft Teams as a central hub for collaboration, approval requests can seamlessly integrate into Teams channels or chats. When notified within Teams, approvers can: View the request details directly in the Teams interface. Approve or reject the request without leaving the platform. Add comments to explain their decision or provide further input. This method is perfect for Teams users, keeping approvals within their workflow to reduce disruptions and improve communication. Responding via the Power Automate app For those employees who need to manage approvals while on the move, the Power Automate mobile app offers a highly convenient solution. Through the app, approvers can: Access a comprehensive list of all pending approval requests. Review the details of each request to make informed decisions. Approve or reject requests with just a tap, ensuring quick responses. Add comments if extra context or clarification is necessary. This option is perfect for users who are frequently away from their desks but still need to stay connected and responsive to approval workflows. By offering multiple ways to respond, whether through email, Microsoft Teams, or the Power Automate app, the approval process becomes more flexible, efficient, and tailored to the diverse needs of today’s workforce. Responding via SharePoint For organizations that utilize SharePoint as a central hub for document management and workflows, approval requests can be accessed and managed directly within the platform. When notified of an approval request in SharePoint, approvers can: Locate the request by navigating to the designated approval list or library where the request is stored. Review the details of the request, including any attached files or supporting information. Approve or reject the request using the built-in approval options available in the SharePoint interface. Add comments to provide feedback or clarify their decision. This method is useful for teams that rely on SharePoint for collaborative work and document tracking, as it keeps the approval process integrated with their existing workflows and resources. Responding via Microsoft Forms In some workflows, approval requests may be routed through Microsoft Forms, providing a structured and user-friendly way to gather responses. When using Forms to respond to an approval request, approvers can: Access the form via a link provided in the notification email or shared directly with them. Review the request details presented within the form, including any relevant context or attached information. Submit their decision by selecting the appropriate option (for example, Approve or Reject) within the form. Add comments in designated fields to provide more feedback or context for their response. This method is effective for workflows that require standardized input or when approvals are part of a broader data collection process. It ensures consistency while remaining simple and accessible for approvers.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Which of these are valid categories of desktop flow actions in Power Automate? (Select all that apply)
explanation: Based on your specific needs, there are many different types of actions. Let’s examine some of the more common categories of desktop flow actions: File and folder actions: You would use these actions to automate file system operations, such as Creating folders, Copying, Deleting, and Moving files. Web automation actions: These actions automate browser tasks without backend API access, like launching a browser, clicking links, and extracting web page data. UI automation actions: Used to interact with desktop applications through their user interface, such as clicking a UI element, or populating a text field. Excel actions: These actions are used to automate Excel data processing. They include tasks such as launching the Excel application, reading data from a worksheet, or writing data to a cell. Email actions: These actions are used to automate email communication and processing such as sending and receiving emails from Outlook. System actions: These actions are used to control system-level operations. They include tasks such as launching applications, shutting down or restarting a PC, or displaying messages. Conditionals and loops: These actions are used to add logic and repetition to desktop flows, such as If statements, and for each loop. Variables and data manipulation: These actions are used to store and manipulate data during flow execution, such as setting variables, and text operations. Scripting and custom code: These actions are used to extend the functionality of a desktop flow with custom scripts such as running Python scripts, and JavaScript code. References: Describe actions for Power Automate desktop flows - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: An organization is losing customers due to slow response times. How could process mining in Power Automate help tackle this?

options.text: By integrating CRM systems for better customer data management
By analyzing customer service processes to identify delays and inefficiencies

explanation: Analyzing customer service processes to identify delays and inefficiencies is the correct choice because process mining in Power Automate allows organizations to visually map out their processes, identify bottlenecks, and optimize workflows. By pinpointing where delays occur in customer service processes, the organization can make necessary improvements to reduce response times and ultimately decrease customer churn.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Which process-mining feature in Power Automate is most useful for spotting bottlenecks in a business process?

options.text: Integrating with external databases for data storage
Providing automated suggestions for process improvements
Generating process maps with visual representations of task flows

explanation: Generating process maps with visual representations of task flows is the most useful feature for identifying bottlenecks in a business process. Visual process maps allow users to see the flow of tasks, identify areas of congestion or delay, and pinpoint where bottlenecks are occurring. This visual representation helps in understanding the process flow and making informed decisions for process optimization. Visualize processes: Process mining generates process maps that show the exact flow of tasks, including variations and deviations. For example, you can see how a purchase order moves through different departments and identify where delays occur. Customize reports: You can create tailored reports to focus on specific metrics, such as processing times or error rates, helping you track performance in key areas. Compare workflows: Process mining allows you to compare different versions of a workflow to identify which one is more efficient. For instance, you could compare how two teams handle customer support tickets and adopt the best practices from the more efficient team. Monitor Key Performance Indicators (KPIs): With built-in dashboards, you can track KPIs like cycle time, throughput, or compliance rates, ensuring your processes align with business goals. Describe process mining - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A small business wants to automate getting notified whenever a new customer fills out a form on their website. What components should their Power Automate flow include?
explanation: A trigger starts the flow (form submission), connectors link to services, and actions send notifications. A and C miss key components. Words from Learning path: Power Automate provides several core components to handle any type of automation needs. This learning unit introduces key concepts like triggers, actions, and connectors, helping you understand how to initiate and manage flows effectively. Triggers, actions, and connectors work together to automate tasks across different systems. Let's look at them more closely: Triggers: Initiate a flow based on specific events, such as receiving an email or adding a file to SharePoint. Actions: Define the tasks the flow performs after being triggered, such as sending a notification, saving a file, or updating a record. Connectors: Act as bridges between Power Automate and external applications, enabling triggers and actions to interact with tools like Outlook, SharePoint, Teams, Salesforce, and more. For example, a flow could use the Outlook connector to trigger when a new email arrives, then use the OneDrive connector to save the attachment and the Teams connector to notify your team. Describe how Power Automate cloud flows use connector triggers and actions - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: As a Power Platform developer, your manager asks: which scenario is the best fit for using a cloud flow template in Power Automate?

options.text: A. When you need to write custom code for a unique automation task
B. When you need a quick start with a prebuilt flow that can be customized
C. When integrating legacy desktop applications with cloud services

explanation: Templates are for quick starts with customization. A requires custom coding, not templates. C is more about desktop flows, not cloud templates. Benefits of using cloud flow templates Cloud flow templates offer several advantages that make them an excellent starting point for automating tasks efficiently: Save time with prebuilt solutions: Cloud flow templates save time by providing prebuilt workflows. For example, if you need to automatically save email attachments to OneDrive, you can select a prebuilt template that handles this task with minimal setup. User-friendly and accessible: These templates feature intuitive interfaces that guide you through the setup process step by step. Even if you’re new to automation, you can easily follow the instructions to customize a template for your specific needs. For instance, a template might prompt you to specify which email sender triggers an action or where files should be saved. Seamless integration with popular applications: Cloud flow templates work effortlessly with widely used tools like Microsoft 365, Slack, SharePoint, and Dataverse. This compatibility allows you to connect different systems and streamline workflows across your organization. For example, you can use a template to send a Slack notification whenever your manager emails you in Microsoft Outlook, ensuring timely communication without manually checking your inbox. Describe use cases for cloud flow templates - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: You're setting up a new Dataverse environment for a multinational company, and the IT team wants to stay compliant with data-residency laws while still allowing global access. Which of these statements are correct? (Select all that apply)

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A sales manager wants a flow that automatically sends a follow-up email 3 days after a customer inquiry if there's been no response. Which components are needed to build this? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. An automated trigger that starts when a new inquiry is received.
B. A scheduled trigger that runs every 3 days.
C. A delay action to wait 3 days before checking for a response.
D. A condition to verify whether the customer has replied.
E. A manual instant trigger to send followups when the manager clicks a button.

explanation: A. True → The flow starts with an automated trigger when a new inquiry is received (e.g., a record created in Dataverse or an email received). B. False → A scheduled trigger runs at fixed times, but here we need the flow to start when an inquiry arrives, not on a schedule. C. True → A delay action waits 3 days before continuing the flow. D. True → A condition checks if the customer has responded. If not, the followup email is sent. E. False → An instant trigger would require manual action, which defeats the purpose of automation. section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate

section: Describe features and capabilities of agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio
text: A company is getting ready to deploy a new Copilot Studio agent to production. Which THREE activities are recommended before doing so?

B. Review the generated topics and responses.

D. Publish immediately because AI-generated agents are production ready.
E. Disable analytics to improve performance.

explanation: A. Test the agent before publishing Testing ensures the agent behaves as expected, answers correctly, and triggers actions properly. Without testing, errors or gaps in conversation flow could reach end users, reducing trust and adoption. This is a critical step in validating the agent’s readiness for production. B. Review the generated topics and responses Copilot can generate topics automatically, but these need human review. Reviewing ensures accuracy, alignment with business rules, and compliance with organizational standards. It also helps refine tone, phrasing, and consistency in responses. C. Monitor usage and adoption after deployment Once deployed, monitoring helps track how users interact with the agent. Analytics reveal adoption rates, common queries, and areas where the agent may need improvement. Continuous monitoring ensures the agent evolves with business needs. Why the Other Options Are Incorrect D. Publish immediately because AI-generated agents are production ready False. AI-generated agents are drafts and require testing, review, and validation before production. Skipping these steps risks errors and poor user experience. E. Disable analytics to improve performance False. Analytics are essential for monitoring usage and improving the agent. Disabling analytics removes visibility into adoption and effectiveness, which is counterproductive.

text: Ben is testing Power Automate and has set up an approval to run, but it doesn't seem to have actually sent the approval request. What could explain that?

Approvals are only allowed to be added by an Administrator

explanation: When Approvals are used for the first time in a Power Automate environment, they need to be initialized. This setup process creates the necessary infrastructure behind the scenes to support approval flows. If this initialization hasn’t occurred, approval requests won’t be sent or processed correctly. Why others are wrong: He does not have an approval license: Power Automate approvals are included in most standard licenses like Microsoft 365. Approvals must be turned on in the Power Platform Admin center: There's no toggle to "turn on" approvals in the Admin center. Initialization happens automatically when approvals are first used. Approvals are only allowed to be added by an Administrator: Any user with access to Power Automate can create approval flows. Admin privileges are not required.

Why Other Options Are Incorrect There is no standalone application for administering Power Automate. Administration is not limited to one method; it can be done through multiple approaches depending on user needs. section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: You're designing a Power Platform solution for Woodgrove Bank and need to explain connector data sources to the team. What are the two types of data sources that Power Platform connectors give you access to? (Select all that apply)
explanation: Correct Answer Function-based data and Tabular data Explanation Power Platform connectors provide access to two types of data sources: Tabular Data Returns information in a structured table format. Example: Excel, SQL tables, SharePoint lists. Best for scenarios where you need to query, filter, or display rows and columns of data. Function-based Data Interacts with data through functions or operations. Can return tabular data but also perform actions such as sending emails, updating calendars, or retrieving user profiles. Function-based data sources → perform actions or return data via functions (Office 365 Users, Azure Blob Storage). Focus on how connectors enable apps and flows to interact with both types of data. section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: As a Power Platform developer, you're moving a CRM solution from development into test. After customizing tables, fields, workflows, and the UI, what type of solution does it become once imported into the test environment?
explanation: Correct Answer Managed Explanation In the Power Platform, Solutions are packages that contain components such as tables, fields, apps, flows, and site maps. They are used to extend or modify the Dataverse database and can be distributed across environments. There are two types of solutions: Unmanaged Solutions Created in the development environment. Developers can freely modify components. Used during the build and refinement phase. Managed Solutions Created by exporting an unmanaged solution and importing it into a test or production environment. Once imported, the solution becomes managed and cannot be modified directly. Ensures stability, integrity, and controlled deployment. When deleted, all customizations and extensions included are removed. Example Suppose you build a custom table for tracking customer feedback in your CRM system: In development, you refine the table structure within an unmanaged solution. When ready for deployment, you package and import it into production. At this point, it becomes a managed solution, ensuring consistency and preventing accidental changes. Key Snippets to Remember for PL-900 Customizations in development = unmanaged layer. Export unmanaged → import into another environment = managed layer. Managed solutions cannot be imported into the same environment as their originating unmanaged solution. Testing managed solutions requires a separate environment. Deleting a managed solution removes all its customizations. Exam Tip For PL-900, focus on: Difference between managed vs unmanaged solutions. How solutions are packaged and moved between environments. Best practices for Application Lifecycle Management (ALM).

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Your model-driven app holds critical sales data, customer details, and transaction history, and your sales team needs it to manage leads, opportunities, and customer relationships. Security matters a lot here, you want only authorized teammates to have access, matched to their role. As you prepare to share the app, which TWO standard security roles could you assign to control that access? (Select all that apply)
explanation: The correct answer is System Customizer & System Administrator When you are ready to share your Power Apps model-driven app, you can select your app and push Share on the screen’s top button bar on the Apps screen. It will open a new panel to choose the people that you want to share your application with. Because a model-driven app is based on Common Data Service (Microsoft Dataverse), you need to assign role-based access to the data. By default, the “Assign a security role” drop-down provides three roles: Environment Maker System Administrator System Customizer Here's a simple explanation of the capabilities of the Environment Maker, System Administrator, and System Customizer roles: Environment Maker: Capability: Environment Makers are like the architects. They can create and set up the working spaces where apps and data live. Example: Imagine them as the ones who design and build the rooms in an office building. System Administrator: Capability: System Administrators are the top-level managers. They have full control and can do things like hiring and firing, managing security, and overall supervision. Example: Think of them as the CEOs who run the entire company. System Customizer: Capability: System Customizers are like interior decorators. They can customize and configure the existing spaces created by Environment Makers to make them more functional and appealing. Example: Picture them as the decorators who arrange the furniture and decorations in each room to suit specific needs. In essence, Environment Makers create the spaces, System Administrators manage everything, and System Customizers fine-tune the details to make the spaces work best for the users. Exam Tips: When it comes to the examination, you should be familiar with the capabilities of each of these three roles. References: Configure user security in an environment - Power Platform | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: As an IT manager, you've built a powerful canvas app to improve internal operations, and it needs to reach critical data sitting in your company's on-premises SQL Server, physically located in your office. What would you use to securely connect the canvas app to that on-prem SQL Server?
explanation: To access on-premises data sources such as SQL Server or SharePoint from the Power Platform, you must configure a data gateway. The gateway acts as a secure bridge between your local network and Microsoft cloud services, enabling apps and flows to interact with on-premises data without exposing it directly to the internet. Canvas apps can connect to SQL Server using the SQL Server connector. If the SQL Server is hosted on-premises, the connector requires a configured data gateway. The gateway ensures secure communication and compliance while allowing seamless integration. Steps to Use a Data Gateway Install the Data Gateway on your local network. Configure the gateway in Power Platform (e.g., Power Pages or Power Apps). Use the SQL Server connector to establish a secure connection between your app and the on-premises database. Key Points for PL-900 Exam Data Gateway = secure access to on-premises data. Required for SQL Server, SharePoint, and other local sources. Cloud-based sources (like Azure SQL) do not require a gateway. Focus

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You're building a Power App for the sales team, and they've asked for a button that emails a proposal to a client. What type of flow would you build to support that?
explanation: The correct answer is Instant Flow. Power Automate provides five types of flows: Automated: This cloud flow type is triggered by an event, like when an email comes from your manager. Instant : This cloud flow type is triggered manually, like when you push a button. Schedule : This cloud flow type is triggered on a schedule, like sending a report of every working data at 8 a.m. Desktop : This flow type automates processes on your desktop. Business process flow: This flow type guides users step-by-step through the business process.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: The maintenance department wants a Power Apps application that includes a flow for field technicians: when a technician needs a part, the mobile app should walk them through searching for and ordering it for delivery. What type of flow fits this?
explanation: The correct answer is Business Process Flow. Reason: A mobile app should take technicians through the step-by-step process of checking if the part is in stock and ordering it for delivery. This type of flow is Business process flow. A Business Process Flow (BPF) provides a structured, step-by-step guide for users to follow a predefined sequence of tasks or stages. In this scenario, where field technicians need guidance in searching for and ordering parts, a BPF ensures consistency and efficiency in the workflow. Power Automate provides five types of flows: Automated: This cloud flow type is triggered by an event, like when an email comes from your manager. Instant: This cloud flow type is triggered manually, like when you push a button. Schedule:  This cloud flow type is triggered on a schedule, like sending a report of every working data at 8 a.m. Desktop: This flow type automates processes on your desktop. Business process flow: This flow type guides users step-by-step through the business process. The key advantages of using Business Process Flows are Guided Workflow: Business process flows provide step-by-step guidance to users, ensuring that they follow a predefined sequence of actions or tasks. Consistency: They promote consistency in how various team members or departments handle specific processes, reducing errors and variations. Efficiency: Business process flows streamline workflows, leading to faster task completion and reduced manual effort. Visibility: They offer visibility into the progress of a process, allowing managers and stakeholders to track and monitor each stage. Training and Onboarding: Business process flows can serve as training tools for new employees, helping them learn how to perform tasks correctly. Automation: They can be integrated with automation tools, triggering actions or notifications at specific points in the process. Collaboration: Business process flows often involve multiple users or departments collaborating on a task, making them useful for cross-functional processes. Exam Success Strategy: To succeed in the PL-900 exam, it's crucial to understand that it doesn't primarily measure your expertise in complex tasks like app development, workflow automation, dashboard design, or chatbot creation. Instead, the key to passing lies in your solid grasp of the fundamental concepts, functionalities, capabilities, and dos and don'ts within the Power Platform ecosystem. For the PL-900 exam, focus on: Understanding the five flow types in Power Automate. How Business Process Flows improve structured workflows. Best practices for designing business process automation. References: Business process flows overview - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: As an IT administrator at Wayne Enterprises, your manager wants separate spaces set up for testing versus production apps and data. Which Power Platform feature lets Wayne Enterprises create both test and production environments like this?
explanation: What is an environment in Power Platform? An environment is a dedicated space within Power Platform where your organization can store, manage, and share apps, data, flows, and chatbots. It acts as a container that helps separate solutions based on their purpose, security needs, or target audience. Use cases include: Hosting all apps in a single environment Creating separate environments for test and production Assigning environments to specific teams or departments Separating environments for global business branches What makes environments suitable for managing test and production apps? Environments can be configured independently, making them ideal for creating test and production versions of apps and databases. This allows teams to safely build and validate solutions in one environment before deploying them live in another. What is environment scope? Environment scope refers to the boundaries and restrictions tied to each environment. This includes: Tenant Isolation: Each environment is created under a specific Azure AD tenant and is accessible only to users within that tenant. Geographic Binding: The environment is tied to a geographic location (e.g., United States), and all associated resources like apps, flows, databases which are hosted in datacenters in that region. Data Access Restriction: Apps in an environment can only connect to data sources that reside within the same environment. Example: An app in the “Test” environment can only connect to the “Test” Dataverse database, not the “Dev” database. Can environments share or move resources? Yes. While environments are isolated by default, you can move resources between them. This supports app lifecycle needs like deploying from test to production. What is the role of Microsoft Dataverse in environments? Each environment can have zero or one Dataverse database, which acts as the storage layer for your apps and chatbots. Whether you can create a Dataverse database depends on: Your Power Apps license Your permission level in the environment What are the types of environments? Power Platform offers several environment types, each suited to different scenarios. What is the default environment? The default environment is automatically created for each Azure AD tenant. It’s shared by all users within the tenant New Power Apps users are added to the Maker role automatically The environment is created in the region closest to the tenant’s default location

section: Describe features and capabilities of agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio
text: Your team deals with repetitive, error-prone data entry every time a project kicks off, hurting both efficiency and accuracy. Which Power Platform tool would streamline this and cut down on errors?
explanation: The correct answer is Power Automate. If you understand the applications of various applications, you will be able to answer the question. Power Apps: Expense Reporting App: Create a mobile app where employees can easily enter and submit their expenses, including receipts and details, streamlining the expense reporting process. Customer Feedback Form: Build a form-based app for collecting customer feedback, which can be accessed by support teams to improve services and products. Inventory Management: Develop an app to track inventory levels, automate reorder notifications, and manage stock across different locations efficiently. Approval Process Automation: Design an automated approval workflow for purchase requests, where managers can review and approve requests with a single click. Data Integration: Create a workflow that extracts data from one application (e.g., SharePoint) and updates it in another (e.g., CRM), ensuring data consistency. Power Copilot Studio: Customer Support Chatbot: Build a virtual agent to assist customers with common inquiries, such as tracking orders, troubleshooting issues, and accessing FAQs. HR Assistant: Create a virtual agent for employees to ask HR-related questions, such as vacation requests, benefits information, or onboarding procedures. Employee Training Portal: Create a  page for employees to enrol in training courses, track their progress, and access learning resources. Community Forum: Build a community pages for users to engage in discussions, share knowledge, and collaborate on topics related to your products or services. These use cases demonstrate how each component of the Power Platform can be applied to various business scenarios, improving efficiency, automation, data analysis, and customer engagement.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Adding an item in SharePoint causes a Power Automate workflow to kick off. What type of operation is being used to start that workflow?
explanation: The correct answer is Trigger. Trigger: In Power Automate (formerly known as Microsoft Flow), a "Trigger" is a specific event that initiates a workflow when it occurs. In the scenario described, the new item added to SharePoint serves as the trigger that starts the workflow. Action: While "Action" is an essential part of a workflow, it's not used to initiate the workflow itself. Actions are steps within the workflow that perform specific tasks after the workflow has been triggered. Function-based: "Function-based" is not a commonly used term in the context of triggering workflows in Power Automate. Triggers and actions are the primary building blocks of workflows in Power Automate. Therefore, "Trigger," is the correct choice as it accurately describes the operation used to start a workflow in response to a specific event, such as adding an item in SharePoint. Exam Tip: For the PL-900 exam, focus on: Understanding the difference between triggers and actions. How Power Automate automates business processes using triggers. Best practices for integrating SharePoint with workflows.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A client wants to use Power Platform to improve their business processes, but is worried about connecting it to their custom API, which their operations depend on. How should you respond to reassure them and explain how Power Platform handles this kind of integration?

options.text: The Power Platform offers the ability to create custom connectors for this purpose, which allow you to connect to Power Apps and Power Automate.
The Power Platform has over 270 connectors to use in these situations.
The Power Platform uses connectors that hold a series of functions available for developers.

explanation: The correct answer is The Power Platform offers the ability to create custom connectors for this purpose, which allow you to connect to Power Apps and Power Automate. This answer is correct because it addresses the client's concerns directly. Custom connectors can be created in Power Platform, enabling seamless integration with external APIs, including custom ones. It's crucial to grasp why the other choices are incorrect, not just to identify the correct one. This helps enhance your knowledge and decision-making during the exam to eliminate incorrect answers. The Power Platform has over 270 connectors to use in these situations: While it's true that Power Platform offers a wide range of pre-built connectors, this option does not specifically address the client's concern about their custom API. Custom connectors are often needed for unique integration scenarios. The Power Platform uses connectors that hold a series of functions available for developers: This statement is a bit technical and doesn't directly assure the client about the ability to interact with their custom API. It focuses on the technical aspects of connectors rather than addressing the client's concern. How to Create a Custom Connector: Access Power Automate or Power Apps. Navigate to "Custom Connectors" under Data or API settings. Define the API URL, authentication method, and request parameters. Test and deploy the connector for seamless integration. Exam Tip: For the PL-900 exam, focus on: Understanding how custom connectors bridge external APIs with Power Platform apps. The difference between built-in connectors and custom connectors.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: A colleague built a model-driven app on Common Data Service to track computer hardware assets and their prices, and worries users might enter wrong values into fields, say, the wrong cost center, when creating a record. How could that be prevented?

options.text: Use Power Automate to validate that the field value matches what the table is expecting.
Use Business Rules to automatically validate the cost centre for the currently -logged-in user.
Use a Canvas App instead of a Model-driven app.

explanation: The correct answer is to use Business Rules to automatically validate the cost centre for the currently -logged-in user. Use business rules. Business rules can be used to automate tasks and enforce business logic. For example, you could create a business rule that checks the cost centre field and prevents the record from being saved if the value is not valid. Other ways of preventing this are as follows: Use data validation rules. Data validation rules can be used to restrict the values that can be entered into a field. For example, you could create a rule that only allows numbers to be entered into the cost centre field. Educate users. It is important to educate users about the correct way to use the app. This includes explaining the data validation rules and business rules that are in place. Here are some additional tips: Use clear and concise labels for all fields. Make sure that the field sizes are appropriate for the data that they are collecting. Use a consistent format for all fields. Consider using a color-coding system to highlight incorrect values.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Say your project requires a mobile app where you need complete control over the user experience and design. Which type of Power Apps app should you build to meet that need?
explanation: The correct answer is the Canvas App. Key features of Canvas, Model Driven and Power Pages for better understanding. Exam Tips: Focus on: Canvas Apps vs. Model-Driven Apps: Understand their differences and when to use each. Power Automate Basics: Learn how automation enhances business processes. Microsoft Dataverse: Know how it supports data storage and relationships. Power Pages: Know to create sites using power pages. section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: You're building a model-driven app for Vertex Logistics, meant for the Dispatch team to log delivery details. Your instructor, Dr. Kumar, asks: what feature of model-driven apps makes sure they display properly across different devices?
explanation: Responsive design - Model-driven apps automatically adjust to different screen sizes and devices, making them ideal for both desktop and mobile use. Why the others are wrong: Custom themes: Control visual branding, not layout responsiveness. Dynamic layouts: Not a native feature of model-driven apps more applicable to manual UI design in canvas apps. Adaptive algorithms: Sound fancy, but not a real component of Power Apps’ responsiveness.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: You're designing a model-driven app for BlueRiver Travel, meant for the Sales team to manage customer bookings. A client, Sophia, asks: what kinds of applications are model-driven apps typically used for?
explanation: Management applications -  Model-driven apps are commonly used to manage operations like case tracking, customer support, resource scheduling, and analytics dashboards. Why the Other Options Are Wrong Gaming applications Require custom graphics, animations, and complex logic. Model-driven apps are designed for structured data management, not interactive gaming experiences. Social media applications Depend on highly dynamic UIs, real-time feeds, and multimedia features. Model-driven apps focus on structured forms, views, and dashboards, not social networking functionality. E-commerce applications While parts (like product inventory or order tracking) could be built in model-driven apps, full e-commerce solutions demand flexible front-end design and customer-facing features. These are better suited to canvas apps or custom development for rich UI and shopping experiences. References: Explore model-driven app features - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Orion Digital is putting together a new model-driven app for the HR team to manage employee records. The IT team asks: what design approach do model-driven apps follow?
explanation: Data-first design Model-driven apps prioritize the data model. The structure of your Dataverse tables determines the app’s layout and logic, not the other way around. Why the Other Options Are Wrong Code-first design Model-driven apps require little to no coding. They emphasize configuration and declarative design over custom development. UI-first design This applies to canvas apps, where makers manually design the interface first and then connect data sources. Model-driven apps automatically generate UI based on the data model. Workflow-first design More relevant to automation tools like Power Automate. Model-driven apps are not designed around workflows; they are designed around data tables and relationships. Resources

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Fill in the blank: __ includes apps that integrate into Microsoft 365, Power Apps, and Power Platform services. (Clue: it's the name of a marketplace.)
explanation: AppSource is Microsoft’s official marketplace for discovering, trying, and acquiring business apps that integrate with Microsoft 365, Power BI, Power Apps, and the rest of the Power Platform. It offers both Microsoft and partner-developed solutions that can enhance workflows, analytics, and overall business productivity. AppSource is intended for business users looking for plug-and-play solutions that work within Microsoft's ecosystem without requiring deep technical setup. Microsoft Marketplace | cloud solutions, AI apps, and agents Azure Marketplace is a marketplace specifically geared toward IT professionals and developers. It offers cloud-based solutions such as virtual machines, databases, machine learning services, and developer tools that are designed to run on Microsoft Azure. While it is similar to AppSource in that it’s a Microsoft marketplace, its focus is on infrastructure and platform solutions, not app integrations with Microsoft 365 or Power Platform. Power Automate is a Power Platform service that helps users create automated workflows between Microsoft services and third-party apps. It is a productivity tool, not a marketplace. While users can browse templates and connectors within Power Automate, it does not provide a catalog of third-party business apps like AppSource does. Instead, it focuses on task automation like sending alerts, moving data, or scheduling activities. Dataverse is the underlying data platform for the Power Platform. It enables secure data storage, standardized data schema, and integration across Power Apps, Power Automate, and other services. It is not a marketplace but rather a backend data service that supports app building and automation. Dataverse helps unify business data, but it doesn’t offer downloadable or installable apps like AppSource.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: At EduTech Academy, the IT team wants to enforce certain rules on their Dataverse tables without writing custom code. What's one of the main advantages of using business rules in Dataverse for this?

options.text: They allow users to enforce logic without custom coding
They're only applicable to model-driven apps
They require Power Fx for implementation

explanation: Enforcing logic without coding is correct because business rules provide a no-code way to apply logic. Only applicable to model-driven apps is wrong because business rules can apply across Dataverse. Require Power Fx is wrong because business rules don’t need formulas; they’re configured visually.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Fill in the blank: __ is the process of proving you're who you say you are, achieved by verifying the identity of a person or device.
explanation: Understand the sequence:Always remember authentication comes before authorization. First you prove who you are, then the system checks what you're allowed to do. Focus on the keyword "identity":If the question talks about proving identity, it's authentication.If it talks about accessing resources or permissions, it's authorization. Don't confuse MFA with the process itself:Multifactor Authentication is a security enhancement to authentication, not a standalone identity check. It’s a method, not the definition. Associate examples with each term:Think of real-life scenarios: Authentication: Logging in with a password. Authorization: Being allowed to view but not edit a file. MFA: Logging in with a password + a code sent to your phone.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Still working on that model-driven app for BlueRiver Travel's Sales team to manage customer bookings, Sophia asks: what's the primary data source model-driven apps rely on?
explanation: Microsoft Dataverse → Model-driven apps are built with a data-first approach and rely exclusively on Dataverse as their data source. Dataverse defines the tables, relationships, and business logic that shape the app’s layout and functionality. Why the others are wrong: SQL Server: While it’s a powerful data source, model-driven apps in Power Platform don't build directly on SQL Server. Excel spreadsheets: More relevant for canvas apps or Power BI not model-driven apps. SharePoint lists: Common for canvas apps, but not valid for building model-driven apps.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A global organization is building a Power Platform solution that connects several business applications, Dataverse, Salesforce, and SQL Server, used across departments. Management wants: users only seeing data relevant to their role; sensitive data never shared with non-approved services; only approved connectors used in production; and environment-level control enforced for makers and admins. Which Power Platform features should be configured to meet all of this? (Select 3)
explanation: A. Security Roles in DataverseSecurity roles define what data users can access and what actions they can perform within Dataverse. This ensures users only see data relevant to their job responsibilities, supporting role-based access control. B. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) PoliciesDLP policies control which connectors can be used together and help prevent sensitive data from being shared with non-approved or risky services like personal or third-party apps. This ensures data compliance and security. C. Environment RolesEnvironment roles control access at the environment level, such as who can be an administrator, maker, or user. This ensures proper governance and limits who can create or manage resources in environments.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: You're planning a Power Apps app that needs to read and write data from SharePoint and OneDrive for Business. Which type of app should you build?
explanation: A canvas app connects to multiple data sources including SharePoint and Excel files stored in OneDrive for Business by using out-of-the-box connectors. Model-driven apps can use only Microsoft Dataverse as the underlying data store. Power Apps portals allow external customers and partners to access data in Microsoft Dataverse. Business process flows are used to standardize business processes, providing a streamlined UI for users to complete a process. Model-driven apps, Power Pages and Business process flows cannot be used to read and write data from SharePoint and OneDrive. Note: Microsoft rebranded Power Apps Portals as Power Pages to better reflect the tool’s capabilities for building websites rather than just portals. The new name emphasizes the web design aspect while still supporting business-centric applications. It is also part of Microsoft's strategy to simplify and streamline the naming of its Power Platform products. section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: A company uses Power Platform, and you need to recommend a use case for formulas in canvas apps. Which TWO actions would you recommend? (Each answer is a complete solution on its own.)

options.text: Save data when a user selects a button.
Change the layout of the app dynamically
Grant or revoke access to data sources

explanation: FILTER is a common formula used in canvas apps to restrict the rows from a data source or collection. The OnSelect property for a button contains the actions to perform. Formulas such as SubmitForm and Patch are used to save data to a data source. Formulas are not used to share a canvas app. Formulas can only be used when building a canvas app. There is no equivalent formula for the WEBSERVICE Excel function that retrieves XML data from an internet URL. section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: A company wants to streamline new-employee onboarding, and needs new hires to manage their active certifications and work history using an Excel workbook. Which Power Apps solution fits this?
explanation: Canvas Apps are perfect for customizing user experience and connecting to a variety of data sources, including Excel on OneDrive or SharePoint. Model Driven Apps require data stored in Dataverse and are best when business logic and relationships are critical. Microsoft Dataverse is a powerful backend but doesn't directly support Excel as a front-end interface. Exam Tips: Choose Canvas Apps when working with Excel files or non-Dataverse data sources. Remember that Model Driven Apps are tightly coupled with Dataverse. If the scenario involves custom UI and Excel, Canvas Apps are the correct choice. Know the distinction between tools (Apps) and data platforms (like Dataverse). text: You need to build a new model-driven app for a different group of users, and it must restrict which table columns users are allowed to change. Which TWO actions would you take? (Each answer is part of the full solution.)

B. Assign security roles with appropriate table privileges

Assign security roles with appropriate table privilegesSecurity roles define table-level permissions such as read, write, create, and delete. Assigning the correct security role ensures users only have the required access to modify data in the model-driven app. Why the other options are incorrect C. Power BI dashboardsPower BI is used for reporting and visualization, not for controlling data modification in apps. D. Create a canvas app instead of a model-driven appChanging the app type does not address column-level security requirements. E. section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A company plans to transform its business using Power Platform and Dataverse. It needs a central backend solution, connected to Dataverse, that managers and staff can use to manage day-to-day business activities, and it must include process guidance so everyone follows the same procedures. Which solution meets this?
explanation: Model-driven applications are used to create backend applications connected to Dataverse. They are typically used by management and other employees and can include business process flows for providing guidance to employees. Canvas applications are used to create applications targeted at specific scenarios. Desktop flows are used to create robotic process automations that automate manual tasks typically done by end users. Power Pages sites provide external users access to Dataverse data. They use model-driven application forms and views to display information to external users.
