section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You need a Power Automate flow that lets managers approve or deny vacation requests. Which TWO flow types would work for this? (Each answer is a complete solution on its own.)
explanation: Business process flows can be used to allow managers to approve or deny vacation requests. Cloud flows can be used to allow managers to approve or deny vacation requests. Desktop flows are used for robotic process automation (RPA). Flow templates are templates, not real flows. Why these two? Business process flows ensure every request follows the same stages and prompts the manager for approval or rejection at the right step. Automated (cloud) flows can watch for new or updated vacation-request records and send out approval cards (via email or Teams) automatically, then update the request based on the manager’s response. Exam Tip: For any approval scenario, pair a business process flow (to enforce the stages and UI guidance) with an automated cloud flow (to handle notifications and update records without manual intervention). section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You're building a Power Automate flow that needs to loop through every row in an Excel spreadsheet and update the first column with today's date for each one. Which action would you configure for this?
explanation: The Apply to each action allows to loop through items in a collection. In this case, this action can be used to loop through each of the rows in the spreadsheet. Do until allows you to loop through items until a specified condition is met. In this scenario, there is no condition, and every item must be looped through. Switch allows taking an input parameter and performing different steps based on the input’s value. In this case, there are no separate actions to take, but the same action to perform on every single row in the spreadsheet. The condition action allows setting up a conditional statement and then perform an action based on whether the condition is true or false. In this scenario, there is no condition to evaluate since every row must be handled the same way. Exam Tip: In your flow, Use the "List rows present in a table" Excel connector to get the rows, then pass the output to “Apply to each,” and within it. Use the “Update a row” action to write the current date to the first column. References: Exercise - Create recurring flows - Training | Microsoft Learn Use the apply to each action in Power Automate to loop through an array of items. (contains video) - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A company uses Power Automate to integrate applications, and has a legacy application with no API at all. Which type of flow would let you access data inside that legacy app?
explanation: Why Desktop Flows? Legacy systems often don’t expose modern APIs or connectors. Desktop Flows use Robotic Process Automation (RPA) to interact with applications through their user interface, mimicking mouse clicks, keyboard input, and reading screen elements. They’re ideal for automating repetitive UI tasks and integrating systems where API integration is not possible. Not suitable: Instant Cloud Flows: Require a trigger and API-based connectors. Scheduled Cloud Flows: Automate tasks based on time, but also rely on API access. Business Process Flows: Guide users through processes in model-driven apps, not for automating legacy system interaction. References: What is Power Automate and the value it brings to you - Training | Microsoft Learn Introduction to desktop flows - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You're building a Power Automate flow that needs to notify a user every time a new item is added to a SharePoint list, and you need to add an email notification step. What would you use?
explanation: This item tests the candidate’s knowledge of Power Automate components such as triggers, actions, conditions, and apply to each loop. Action: Actions in Power Automate are the steps that perform specific tasks, like sending an email. In this case, after the trigger (new item added to a SharePoint list), the action you need is to send an email to notify the user. This is an essential part of the flow. Triggers: Triggers are used to start the flow, such as when a new item is added to a SharePoint list. However, triggers do not send email notifications; they only initiate the flow. Condition: A condition would be used if you needed to check whether certain criteria are met before performing a specific task. However, in this scenario, you simply need to notify the user every time a new item is added, so no condition is necessary. Apply to each loop: This loop is used to iterate through a collection of items. Since the task is about notifying the user for each new item (and there is no collection involved), you don't need an "Apply to each" loop in this case. Exam Tips: References: Exercise - Create your first flow - Training | Microsoft Learn Automate tasks by creating a cloud flow - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You need to modify a cloud flow. Which of these approaches could you use to do that?
explanation: This item tests the candidate’s knowledge of modifying a cloud flow. Power Automate portal – Primary place to edit cloud flows Power Apps Studio – You can open/edit flows created from a canvas app Power Automate mobile app – Allows editing basic flow details and management To modify a cloud flow, the correct tools to use are: Power Automate mobile app: This app allows you to modify cloud flows directly from your mobile device, making it convenient for quick changes while on the go. Power Automate portal: The Power Automate portal is the web-based platform that provides a comprehensive set of tools to create, manage, and modify cloud flows. This is the most robust platform for modifying flows. Power Apps Studio: Power Apps Studio is mainly used for building and customizing apps that interact with Power Automate flows. You can modify a cloud flow that is linked to a Power App via this platform, especially when you need to integrate your flow with custom applications. Explanation of Incorrect Options: Copilot Studio: This tool is used for creating chatbots, and while it can integrate with Power Automate, it is not used for modifying cloud flows. Form and data integration It builds forms connected to Dataverse automatically, so site visitors can submit data securely without manual schema setup. Query Building Support → Assists in creating queries without coding. Monitoring Insights → Explains flow run results and suggests fixes when failures occur. text: You're building an app for Titan Logistics, for the Dispatch team to schedule fleet deliveries. Your instructor, Dr. Chen, asks: true or false, in a default environment, Microsoft Entra ID users are given the Environment Maker role.

Grants permission to: Create and manage apps, flows, and other components. Customize solutions within the environment. Does not include full administrative privileges. explanation: The correct option is System Administrator System Administrator Role Grants full administrative control over an environment. Key capabilities include: Add or remove users or groups from Environment Admin or Environment Maker roles. Provision a Dataverse database for the environment. View and manage all resources created within the environment. Set data loss prevention (DLP) policies. Manage environment settings. Other Roles (Incorrect Options) Environment Maker Can create new resources such as apps, connections, custom connectors, gateways, and flows. Can share apps with individuals, security groups, or the entire organization. Cannot access or manage the environment’s data. System Customizer Can create and customize apps, tables (formerly called entities), and security roles in Dataverse. Can view and manage all data in the environment. Dataverse User Can view and interact with data in Dataverse. Cannot create or customize apps, tables, or security roles. Delegate Not a recognized role type in Power Platform. Exam Tips: Know the difference between Environment roles (Admin, Maker) and Dataverse roles (System Administrator, System Customizer, User). Remember that System Administrator has the broadest permissions, including environment-level and Dataverse-level control. Be aware of updated terminology: "tables" instead of "entities." Expect scenario-based questions where you must identify which role is appropriate for a given task. text: As an app maker at CrystalWave Media building a helpdesk-ticket app for IT, your manager Ms. Thompson asks: which are the correct definitions of DPA and RPA? (Select all that apply)

options.text: DPA - It is cloud-based software that helps organize and automate the steps involved in a process.
RPA - It is cloud-based software that helps organize and automate the steps involved in a process.
DPA  - It is software that mimics human interactions with computer systems.
RPA  - It is software that mimics human interactions with computer systems.

explanation: Exam Tips: Use this mnemonic: DPA = Digital Processes (Think workflow, approval chains, business logic) RPA = Robotic Actions (Think clicks, typing, screen scraping) DPA (Digital Process Automation): DPA is like a digital conductor for business tasks. It's software that helps organize and automate the steps involved in a process, such as approving expense reports or processing customer orders. Think of it as a digital assistant that ensures things get done correctly and on time. DPA doesn't mimic human actions; it streamlines digital processes. RPA (Robotic Process Automation): RPA, on the other hand, is like having a robot colleague. It's software that mimics human interactions with computer systems. Imagine a robot at a computer, clicking buttons, copying data, and filling out forms just like a human would. RPA is excellent for repetitive, rule-based tasks where a human would otherwise spend a lot of time doing the same actions. For example, when you do not have an API of a particular software App, you can use the RPA to record the actions and screen scrape them. With desktop flows, they were able to mimic onscreen actions that customer service associates used to perform manually via robotic process automation (RPA). In summary, DPA focuses on automating and optimizing digital processes, while RPA automates tasks by simulating human actions on a computer. Both technologies aim to make work more efficient and less error-prone. References: Describe the capabilities of Power Automate - Training | Microsoft Learn

Guides users through work processes. Ensures tasks are completed according to organizational processes. Provides a clear path to reach conclusions in tasks. Cloud Flows: The most common type of flow. Starts with a trigger (like an email or a social media mention). Includes actions (like creating records or sending approval requests). Automates tasks based on digital triggers and actions. Desktop Flows (Robotic Process Automation - RPA): Record your actions on your computer or web browser. Can be triggered to repeat those actions. Can handle data input and output. Automates tasks, even those that are typically done manually, by mimicking your actions on the computer. In essence, Business Process Flows help guide work processes, Cloud Flows automate tasks triggered by digital events, and Desktop Flows automate tasks on your computer by recording and repeating actions. References: Describe the capabilities of Power Automate - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: While designing an automation in Power Automate, how many triggers can a single flow actually have?

options.text: A flow can have multiple trigger points

explanation: The correct answer is 1. A flow only has one trigger. The trigger serves as the entry point for the flow and determines when the flow should start running. Hence, A flow typically has one trigger because the trigger defines the event or condition that initiates the flow's execution. Advantages of having one trigger: Clarity: It provides a clear and straightforward understanding of when the flow will start. Focused Automation: The flow remains concentrated on a specific event or condition, ensuring accuracy. Ease of Maintenance: Simplifies maintenance and troubleshooting since there's one primary entry point to the flow. Predictable Behavior: This makes the behaviour of the flow predictable, as it responds consistently to the designated trigger. Simplicity: Keeps the flow logic simple and easy to follow for both creators and reviewers. Reduced Complexity: Minimizes the chances of conflicts or unexpected interactions with other flows. Scalability: Allows for scaling automation by creating additional flows with different triggers as needed. Improved Performance: Helps maintain optimal flow performance by reducing unnecessary complexity. Important points to remember: While most flows have one trigger, you can use conditions, actions, and branching logic within the flow to create complex workflows that respond to various conditions or events after the initial trigger. This allows for flexibility and customization in automating business processes. References: Triggers - Describe the components of a cloud flow - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: As an app maker at CrystalWave Media building a helpdesk-ticket app for IT, your manager Ms. Thompson asks: which of these is a type of column in Dataverse?
explanation: Dataverse offers a variety of column types to meet the needs of diverse data storage and manipulation scenarios within the Power Platform. Each column type is designed to store specific types of information, whether it's text, numbers, dates, or more specialized data. All of the above are types of columns in Dataverse. Dataverse provides a variety of column types to support different types of data, including: Text columns: Store text data, such as names, addresses, and descriptions. Number columns: Store numeric data, such as quantities, prices, and dates. Date/time columns: Store date and time data. Choice columns: Store a single value from a list of predefined values. Lookup columns: Store a reference to a record in another table. Currency columns: Store currency data. Boolean columns: Store true/false values. Multi-select picklist columns: Store multiple values from a list of predefined values. Dataverse also supports custom column types, which can be used to store more complex data types, such as images, files, and geographical locations.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: SolarEdge Technologies is building a new app for Inventory to track spare parts. The IT team asks: which of these is a core component of model-driven apps in Power Platform?
explanation: Understand: Flow Templates: These are pre-built templates in Power Automate that help automate business processes, such as sending emails or syncing data between systems. While useful for integrating and automating workflows, they are not the core component of Model-Driven Apps. Power Automate Flows: Power Automate can automate processes in both Canvas and Model-Driven Apps, but they are not a central component of the app structure itself. Be clear on the distinction: Power Automate enhances both types of apps but does not define their core structures like entities do in Model-Driven Apps. Know the Key Components of Model-Driven Apps: Entities (Now called Tables) Role: Core building blocks of the data model. Purpose: Represent business data (e.g., Contacts, Accounts, Cases). Functionality: Define fields (columns) to store structured data. Drive app logic, security, and automation. Support business rules, workflows, and calculated fields. Forms Role: Interface for users to view, create, and edit entity records. Types: Main forms: Full-featured forms for desktop and mobile. Quick create forms: Streamlined for fast data entry. Card forms: Compact views for dashboards or embedded experiences. Customization: Add sections, tabs, business rules, and embedded components. Control visibility and behavior based on user roles or data conditions. Views Role: Display lists of records in a grid format. Functionality: Define which columns are shown and in what order. Include filters and sorting to tailor data presentation. Used in dashboards, subgrids, and lookup fields. Types: Public views: Shared across users. Personal views: Created by individual users for their own use. Relationships Role: Link entities to reflect real-world connections. Types: One-to-many (1:N): One record in Entity A relates to many in Entity B (e.g., one Account has many Contacts). Many-to-one (N:1): Many records in Entity A relate to one in Entity B. Many-to-many (N:N): Records in Entity A can relate to multiple records in Entity B and vice versa. Impact: Enable navigation between related records. Power subgrids, roll-up fields, and related views. References: Explore model-driven applications - Training | Microsoft Learn

Explanation: You can create and manage Dataverse environments through the Power Platform Admin Center. This platform allows admins to configure environments, assign security roles, and monitor resources for Power Apps, Power Automate, and Dataverse. You must enable data encryption after you create a Common Data Service environment. Answer: No Explanation: Data encryption is automatically enabled in Dataverse. Microsoft applies Azure-managed encryption for data stored within Dataverse, meaning users do not need to manually enable it after creating an environment. You can control security rules and privileges in a Common Data Service environment from the Power Apps admin center. Answer: No Explanation: Security rules and privileges for Dataverse are managed in the Power Platform Admin Center, not the Power Apps Admin Center. The Power Platform Admin Center allows administrators to configure role-based security, apply field-level security, and define record-level security. The Power Platform Admin Center allows you to manage environments, assign security roles, and monitor resources for Power Apps, Power Automate, and Dataverse. Security rules and privileges for Dataverse are not managed in the Power Apps Admin Center. The correct place to manage Dataverse security is the Power Platform Admin Center. The Power Platform Admin Center supports role-based security configuration. It also allows for field-level security settings to protect sensitive data. Record-level security can be defined to control access to individual records. The Power Platform Admin Center is the central hub for environment configuration and governance across Power Platform services.

text: At GlobalCorp, admins are planning strict governance across multiple Power Platform environments, sensitive data needs to stay isolated, lifecycle management needs to stay consistent, and developers need to be able to test without touching production. text: Fill in the blank: a business process flow can have no more than __ stages.
explanation: Keep in Mind on Limitations: This might change time to time as MS Updates time to time. Pls refer to the MS Learning paths to know about the latest limitations. This question is purely for information purpose to understand the limitations. This will help you when you build flows. General Power Platform Limits 1) How many API requests can a user make per day? API request limits vary by license. For example, Microsoft 365 users typically get 6,000 requests per 24 hours, while premium licenses offer more. 2) What happens if a flow exceeds its request limits? Flows may be throttled or turned off if they exceed limits continuously for 14 days. Power Automate Limits 1) How many actions can a single flow contain? A flow can have up to 500 actions. Exceeding this may cause performance issues. 2) What is the maximum nesting depth for actions? You can nest actions up to 8 levels deep, such as within conditions or switch cases. 3) How many switch cases are allowed in a flow? A single switch scope can contain up to 25 cases. 4) How many variables can be used in a flow? Each flow can include up to 250 variables. 5) How many flows can a single user own? A user can own up to 600 cloud flows in one environment. 6) What is the maximum run duration for a flow? Flows can run for up to 30 days before being automatically stopped. 7) How long are flow run histories retained? Run data is retained for 30 days from the start time. 8) What happens to dormant flows? Flows not triggered for 90 days may be turned off, especially under Free, Trial, or Microsoft 365 plans. Dataverse Limits 1) How many active business process flows are allowed per table? Each Dataverse table can have up to 10 active business process flows. 2) How many stages can each business process flow contain? Each flow can include up to 30 stages. Environment Limits 1) Is there a limit to the number of environments in Power Platform? There’s no fixed cap, but Dataverse for Teams may have practical limits. Regular environments are constrained by storage capacity, not a hard number. References https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/learn/modules/build-automated-solution/4-build-business-process-flow https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/business-process-flows-overview

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: During a training workshop at NovaTech, the facilitator poses this to participants, true or false: after creating a user-owned custom entity in Dataverse, you can change its ownership from user-owned to organization-owned.
explanation: The correct answer is False. Once an entity is created as user-owned, its ownership type cannot be changed to organization-owned. The ownership type is determined at the time of entity creation and remains fixed. If you need an organization-owned version, you would need to create a new entity with the correct ownership type and migrate data accordingly Dataverse is an important topic in PL900 exam and below are important things to know about Dataverse. What Dataverse IsDataverse is a cloud-based data platform that allows you to securely store and manage data used by business applications. It provides a standardized and scalable data structure. Standard vs. Custom Tables Standard tables (e.g., Contact, Account) come built-in. Custom tables can be created to match your specific business needs. Table Ownership Types Use-Owned: Used when access control is based on who owns the data. Organization-Owned: Used for global data not tied to any individual user. Relationships Between TablesDataverse supports 1:N, N:1, and N:N relationships between tables to model business logic and data relationships. Business RulesBusiness Rules allow you to enforce logic and validation without writing code, right inside Dataverse. Security ModelDataverse uses a role-based security model with: Security Roles Field-level security Record-level security Dataverse and Power AppsPower Apps integrates tightly with Dataverse, letting you easily build model-driven and canvas apps that interact with data. Dataverse and Power AutomateYou can create flows in Power Automate that trigger from Dataverse data changes, such as when a record is created, updated, or deleted. Dataverse Connectors and IntegrationDataverse can integrate with other systems through: Standard connectors Custom connectors Azure integration Dataverse for TeamsA lite version of Dataverse included with Microsoft Teams. It allows you to build apps and flows directly in Teams without requiring a full Power Platform license. References: Update a record Owner and Owning Business Unit - Power Platform | Microsoft Learn Change entity/table scope to user from organization

text: At Evergreen Foods, building an app for Procurement to track supplier invoices, your manager Mr. Daniels stresses integration and asks: true or false, custom connectors can be reused across multiple platforms, including Power Apps, Power Automate, and Azure Logic Apps.
explanation: The correct answer is - True. An advantage of building custom connectors is that they can be used in different platforms, such as Power Apps, Power Automate, and Azure Logic Apps. Here are some other advantages of building custom connectors: Increased flexibility: Custom connectors can be created to connect to any API, regardless of whether it is a public or private API. Reduced development time: Custom connectors can be created using a variety of tools and technologies, including Visual Studio Code and Power Platform CLI. This can help to reduce the development time required to create a custom connector. Improved security: Custom connectors can be secured using OAuth 2.0 and other authentication protocols. This helps to protect the data that is being accessed through the custom connector. If you are looking for a way to connect to a data source that is not natively supported by Power Apps, Power Automate, or Azure Logic Apps, then building a custom connector is a great option. section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: As a Power Apps developer at a mid-sized manufacturing company that's just rolled out Power Platform to improve operations, which common challenges might the organization run into? (Select all that apply)
explanation: The correct answer is  Access to External, third-party services & Exposure of data leakage. Data Validation and Data Synchronization are not issues of data in the Power Platform. Apps and automation are becoming increasingly connected across multiple data sources and multiple services. Some of these might be external, third-party services and might even include some social networks. Users generally have good intentions, but they can easily overlook the potential for exposure from data leakage to services and audiences that should not have access to the data. Create DATA LOSS PREVENTION POLICIES(DLP) that can act as guardrails to help prevent users from unintentionally exposing organizational data. Here are some common related issues that organizations might encounter: Data Leakage and Privacy: Integrating external services or connectors can sometimes inadvertently lead to data leakage if not properly configured. Sensitive information could be exposed unintentionally, risking data privacy and compliance. Unauthorized Access: Improperly configured access controls can lead to unauthorized users gaining access to sensitive data or functionality within the Power Platform applications. Authentication and Authorization: Integrating with third-party services requires proper authentication and authorization mechanisms to ensure that only authorized users and systems can access and manipulate data. Reference Links: Power Platform DLP Policy: Everything You Need To Know - YouTube Data Loss Prevention policy reference | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: True or false: standard tables are also known as out-of-the-box tables.
explanation: The correct answer is True. A Power Platform environment that contains Microsoft Dataverse comes with a number of standard tables, commonly referred to as out-of-the-box tables. Tables in Dataverse that are considered standard include those for accounts, business units, contacts, tasks, and users. The majority of the common tables offered by Dataverse can be altered. Imported tables (Custom tables) that are part of a managed solution and are marked as configurable also show up as standard tables. These tables, where the table property has a customizable set to true, can be customised by any user with the necessary rights. References: Types of tables - Power Apps | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Which cloud-based service lets you build automated workflows across apps and services, sending notifications, syncing files, collecting data, and more?
explanation: The correct answer is Power Automate Flows Power Automate is a cloud-based service that lets you create automated workflows between apps and services to get notifications, sync files, collect data, and more. Power Automate flows enable users to create automated workflows to connect various applications, services, and data sources, allowing for seamless data exchange and task automation. Power Automate flows and Business Process Flows (BPFs) are both integral components of the Microsoft Power Platform, but they serve different purposes and have distinct functionalities within the context of process automation and user guidance.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: True or false: Dataverse environments let you manage user access, security settings, and the storage associated with that database.
explanation: The correct answer is True. Microsoft Dataverse environments allow you to manage user access, security settings, and the storage that is associated with that database. Each environment is created under a Entra ID tenant, and its resources can only be accessed by users within that tenant. Within each environment, you have control over the following: User Access: You can manage who has access to the environment, including administrators, developers, and end-users. Access can be controlled through role-based security and permissions. Security Settings: You can configure security settings to define who can view, create, update, or delete data and records within the Dataverse tables. This includes setting up roles, privileges, and data-sharing rules. Storage Management: Each environment has its own associated Dataverse database, and you can manage the storage allocated to that database. You can monitor storage usage, set up retention policies, and optimize data storage. Solution Deployment: Environments allow you to manage and deploy solutions, which are collections of apps, customizations, and configurations. This enables you to control the deployment of changes across different environments. Integration and Connectivity: Environments can also be configured to integrate with external services, data sources, and APIs, allowing you to extend the functionality of your applications. By providing these capabilities, Microsoft Dataverse environments offer flexibility and control over the development, deployment, and management of applications and solutions while adhering to security and data management requirements. Power Platform environments overview - Power Platform | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Rahmat is building a model-driven app and sharing the same tables with other app designers. He's worried data could get mixed up and compliance with data-protection rules could suffer. Which model-driven Power Apps features help prevent that?

options.text: Environments, Business Units and Multi Factor Authentication.
Business Units, Role Based Security and Conditional Access Policies.
Environments, Role Based Security and Business Units

explanation: The most accurate answer is - Environments, Role Based Security and Business Units Environments: These provide isolation between different stages (e.g., development, testing, production) and between teams or business areas. Each environment has its own Dataverse database, so data is separated. Role Based Security: Ensures that users only access data and functionality they've been explicitly permitted. You define security roles that control access to tables, forms, and records. Business Units: Help structure the organization within Dataverse. You can assign users and records to business units, and use these to restrict access so data isn’t shared across units unless intended. Why others are wrong: Multi Factor Authentication and Conditional Access Policies are more about securing sign-ins than protecting app-level data. Licenses and Admin Roles help with access management at a broader level but don’t control how data is separated or protected inside the app itself.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Leo mentions building a Campaign ROI Assistant for Marketing and says he already knows about automated cloud flows. Maya asks: which scenario best represents a real use case for an automated cloud flow in Power Automate?

options.text: Run a flow when a specific event happens, such as receiving an email or a new item being created in SharePoint.
Trigger a flow to perform a task, such as sending a reminder email at a specific time.
Create a custom form to collect data from users and automatically perform actions based on the responses.
Build a UI-based process to automate a sequence of tasks across multiple apps.

explanation: 1. Automated Cloud Flow Automated Cloud Flows are triggered by a specific event, like an incoming email or new data entry. Use Cases for Automated Cloud Flow: Email notifications: Automatically send an email to a team member when a high-priority email is received. New SharePoint item creation: Trigger actions, such as notifying a manager or logging the data in Excel, when a new item is created in SharePoint. Task creation in Planner: When a new row is added to a specific Excel table, automatically create a task in Planner. New file in OneDrive: Trigger a flow to copy files into a backup folder when a new file is uploaded to OneDrive. New form submission: Automatically collect responses from Microsoft Forms and save them in a SharePoint list or Excel file. 2. Instant Cloud Flow Instant Cloud Flows are manually triggered by the user via a button, for example, in the Power Automate mobile app or within other apps like SharePoint. Use Cases for Instant Cloud Flow: Send reminder emails: Trigger a flow via a button to send reminder emails to a group of users for a meeting. File approval process: Manually approve or reject documents by pressing a button in SharePoint, triggering an approval workflow. Trigger a Power Automate button: Initiate a flow from within a Power Apps app, like submitting a form to create a record in a database. Data clean-up: Trigger a flow that removes or archives old data in a SharePoint list at the click of a button. Send emergency alerts: Press a button in Power Automate to send out urgent notifications via email or Teams chat in case of critical events. 3. Scheduled Flow Scheduled Flows run at specific times or intervals, which you define in the flow settings. Use Cases for Scheduled Flow: Weekly data backup: Automatically back up a database or SharePoint list to another storage system at regular intervals (e.g., every night). Invoice reminders: Send reminders to customers to pay their invoices every month. Monthly report generation: Automatically generate a report every month and email it to stakeholders. System health checks: Run an automated task to check the health of key systems (e.g., ensuring backup jobs ran successfully). Data synchronization: Sync data from one system to another (e.g., from Salesforce to a SQL database) every day at midnight. 4. Business Process Flow Business Process Flows are designed to ensure that users follow a defined set of steps in a process, such as lead qualification in sales or case management. Use Cases for Business Process Flow: Lead qualification in sales: Guide sales reps through the steps to qualify leads (e.g., collecting contact info, evaluating needs, setting appointments). Customer service case management: Ensure customer service agents follow a specific set of actions for case resolution (e.g., initial review, investigation, escalation). Employee onboarding: Manage a sequence of onboarding tasks for new hires, ensuring they complete documents, training, and setup steps in order. Project management workflows: Standardize steps for managing project milestones, from initiation to completion, including approvals and documentation. Incident management: Define the process to investigate and resolve IT issues or security incidents, with steps for escalating and closing cases. 5. UI Flow (Desktop Flow) UI Flows automate tasks on a local desktop application or web interface that doesn't have APIs for integration. Use Cases for UI Flow: Automate repetitive desktop tasks: Automate tasks in desktop apps like Excel, Outlook, or SAP that don’t have direct API access. Fill out web forms: Automate the process of filling out and submitting web forms across various websites for data entry tasks. Data entry automation: Use UI Flows to input data from Excel sheets into a desktop application, like an ERP system, which doesn't support APIs. Automated report generation: Use UI Flows to generate reports in desktop applications by extracting data and compiling reports in specific formats. End-of-day system updates: Trigger the automation of logging into desktop applications, performing routine tasks like checking logs or running updates at the end of the day.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Can you create a Desktop Flow and connect it to a Cloud Flow in Power Automate?

options.text: True - Yes, The whole system can have multiple flows.
False - It is not possible. Desktop flows and Cloud flows are independent.

explanation: The correct answer is True. Many times, a desktop flow is part of a bigger overall automation solution.  Desktop flows are used to simulate user interaction with an application or a website. The whole process is done with a cloud flow. For example, below given a scenario how clod flow and desktop flow can be used together. The cloud flow is triggered automatically when an email is received in the dedicated mailbox in Outlook. AI Builder is used to extract details from the invoice attachment such as the vendor, invoice date, and amount. An approval request is sent to the appropriate person in Microsoft Teams. The request will include the invoice details that were extracted from the invoice. Once the request is approved, the cloud flow will run a desktop flow that was created to interact with the legacy application. The invoice details such as the vendor, invoice date, and amount are used in the creation of the invoice record. Once the invoice is logged, the invoice number is captured and a new email is created in Outlook. The email includes the status of the invoice and the invoice number. section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: What's the main purpose Adaptive Cards serve in digital communication and application interfaces?

options.text: To provide static, unchangeable content to users.
To display complex content exclusively in web applications.
To offer a flexible and platform-agnostic way to present content and interactions.
To replace traditional email attachments with interactive content.

explanation: This topic is not part of the official PL-900 exam scope. It is included here purely for informational purposes to help broaden understanding of the Power Platform ecosystem. The correct answer is - To offer a flexible and platform-agnostic way to present content and interactions. The primary purpose of Adaptive Cards is to provide a flexible and platform-agnostic format for presenting content and user interactions in a consistent manner across various digital communication and application interfaces. Adaptive Cards adapt to the host platform's visual style and capabilities, making them versatile for different use cases and platforms. Why others are wrong: A) To provide static, unchangeable content to users: Adaptive Cards are designed for dynamic content and interactions, so their primary purpose is not to provide static content. B) To display complex content exclusively in web applications: While Adaptive Cards can be used in web applications, they are not limited to web-exclusive use. They are intended to work across different platforms and applications. D) To replace traditional email attachments with interactive content: While Adaptive Cards can be used in email, their purpose goes beyond replacing attachments; they are used to create interactive and adaptable content within messages and applications. References: Consider Power Automate scenarios - Training | Microsoft Learn Create flows that post adaptive cards to Microsoft Teams - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn

text: Leo mentions building a Campaign ROI app for Marketing and says he already knows the difference between Capacity and Environment. Maya asks: in the Power Platform admin center, what actually distinguishes a "Capacity" from an "Environment"?

options.text: Capacities control app design, while environments control data storage.
Capacities determine user access, while environments manage app deployment.
Capacities are used for app hosting, while environments provide isolation for resources and security settings.
Capacities are specific to Canvas Apps, while environments are specific to Model-Driven Apps.

explanation: Why others are wrong? A) Capacities control app design, while environments control data storage: This statement is not accurate. Capacities primarily determine the resources available for app execution, while environments are broader and include data storage, security settings, and resource isolation. B) Capacities determine user access, while environments manage app deployment: While both capacities and environments play a role in user access and app deployment, this statement oversimplifies their roles. Capacities are more about resource allocation, and environments encompass a wider range of settings beyond just app deployment. D) Capacities are specific to Canvas Apps, while environments are specific to Model-Driven Apps: This statement is not correct. Capacities apply to both Canvas Apps and Model-Driven Apps, and they are not limited to a specific app type. Environments can host various types of apps and resources. Option C is the correct answer because it accurately distinguishes between the roles of capacities and environments in the Power Platform Admin Center. Capacities are primarily responsible for app hosting resources, while environments provide isolation for resources and encompass various settings, including security. The PL-900 exam tests knowledge on securing Power Platform environments using the tools below. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) - D. It allows organizations to control who can access and perform specific actions within Power Platform based on their roles. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Policies - A. text: Match each admin center to its primary management focus. Centers: Dynamics 365 admin center, Power Apps admin center, Power Platform admin center, Microsoft 365 admin center. Focus areas: A) Managing business applications, including CRM and ERP solutions. B) Managing custom app environments, connectors, and gateways. C) Overseeing the entire Power Platform, including Power Apps and Power Automate. D) Administering Microsoft 365 services like Exchange, SharePoint, and Teams.
explanation: Dynamics 365 admin center (1 - A): This admin center focuses on managing business applications like Customer Relationship Management (CRM) and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) solutions within the Dynamics 365 ecosystem. Power Apps admin center (2 - B): Here, administrators manage custom app environments, configure connectors for integration with other services, and handle gateways that connect to on-premises data sources. Power Platform admin center (3 - C): This center oversees the entire Power Platform, including Power Apps, Power Automate enabling administrators to manage and configure all these tools from a single point. section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Match each term to its correct description. Terms: Data source, App, Gateway, Flow. Descriptions: A) The user interface and functionality built in Power Apps. B) The external data or databases that Power Apps or Power Automate interacts with. C) Provides secure access to on-premises data sources from Power Apps or Power Automate when needed. D) The automated workflows built in Power Automate to perform tasks.
explanation: Data Source A data source refers to the external data or databases that Power Apps or Power Automate connects to in order to fetch or store information. For example, a SharePoint list or a SQL database can be a data source. App An app in Power Apps represents the user interface and the functionality that is created to interact with users. Apps are designed to allow users to input and view data, often powered by underlying data sources. Gateway A gateway is a tool used to securely connect and access data from on-premises systems (i.e., systems that are not in the cloud) for use in Power Apps or Power Automate. For example, it can be used to connect to a SQL server that is hosted within your organization's network. Flow A flow refers to the automated workflows created in Power Automate. These workflows allow you to automate tasks such as sending emails, updating data, or performing actions based on triggers or conditions. For example, you can create a flow that sends an email every time a new record is added to a SharePoint list. These terms are important because they represent the core components that work together in Power Apps and Power Automate to help you build and automate business processes.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: In an enterprise setting, which scenario is the best fit for implementing attended RPA (Robotic Process Automation)?

options.text: Automating data entry tasks in a highly regulated financial institution
Managing and optimizing server resources in a data centre
Enhancing customer service by implementing AI chatbots
Streamlining the manufacturing process in a car assembly line

explanation: The correct answer is: A) Automating data entry tasks in a highly regulated financial institution. The reason why the other options are wrong is as follows: B) Managing and optimizing server resources in a data center: This scenario is more aligned with unattended RPA, where robots perform tasks independently without human intervention. C) Enhancing customer service by implementing AI chatbots: While chatbots can be considered a form of automation, they are not typically classified as attended RPA, which involves human-in-the-loop automation for tasks that require human judgment or interaction. D) Streamlining the manufacturing process in a car assembly line: This scenario is more related to industrial automation and robotics rather than attended RPA, which is focused on office-based or business process automation. Exam Tips: Know the difference between Attended and Unattended RPA: Attended RPA: Requires human input and is triggered by the user (use cases involving compliance, customer service, etc.). Unattended RPA: Runs without human intervention (use cases involving back-end processes like server management).

text: At Harvest Organics, you're building a Supplier Audit app for Procurement. Your manager, Mr. Daniels, asks: true or false, environment-level DLP policies can't override tenant-wide DLP policies.

These policies are designed to provide additional control and restrictions within that specific environment, but they cannot override or supersede the tenant-wide DLP policies that apply to the entire organization. Tenant-wide DLP policies take precedence over environment-level policies to ensure consistent data protection and compliance across all environments.

text: Orion Finance is building a new Loan Reminder flow for the Risk team. The IT team asks: how do you set up a flow that recurs daily?

Create the flow and set the flow flag frequency to daily reoccurrence

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Every flow is built from two main parts: a trigger, and one or more actions. Which of these best describes what an action is?

options.text: Actions are what you want to happen when a trigger is invoked
Actions will trigger the frequency of the flow reoccurrence
Triggers are what you want to happen when an action is invoked
Flow actions trigger the flow to occur as long as the defined value of the trigger is met.

explanation: In Power Automate (and other flow-based automation tools), every flow consists of two core components: Trigger This is the event that starts the flow. Examples: receiving an email, a new item in SharePoint, a scheduled time. Actions These are the tasks that the flow performs after the trigger is activated. Examples: sending an email, updating a database, creating a task in Planner. Exam Tips: Why people get confused A single flow can use only one trigger (this is true). But a connector itself can expose multiple triggers. Why the Other Options Are Incorrect: Actions will trigger the frequency of the flow reoccurrence Incorrect: Triggers control how often a flow runs. Actions are executed only after a trigger is fired. Triggers are what you want to happen when an action is invoked Incorrect: The flow logic starts with a trigger, not the other way around. Triggers start the process; actions follow. Flow actions trigger the flow to occur as long as the defined value of the trigger is met Incorrect: This confuses the roles. Only the trigger starts the flow; actions just respond once that trigger happens. References: Work with triggers - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You want to get alerted whenever a change is made to a list. How can Power Automate help with this?

options.text: Power Automate can send up a flare near you to alert you of changes
You can write a flow with Power Automate to send push notifications, texts, or emails for various trigger
Sorry, Power Automate can't help with that

explanation: Power Automate is designed exactly for this kind of task, monitoring changes and responding with alerts or actions. How Power Automate Helps: Trigger: Use a trigger like “When an item is created or modified” for a SharePoint list. This watches for any changes to the list. Actions: After the trigger is fired, you can configure actions such as: Send an email to notify team members. Send a push notification to your mobile device. Send a text message using services like Twilio. (Optionally) Post to Teams, update a file, or log the change. Why the Other Options Are Incorrect: Power Automate can send up a flare: Not realistic, clearly a distraction Power Automate can’t help;  it’s built to help with this.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You're designing a Guest Check-In flow for Laguna Resorts. Talking it through with analyst Fatima: what are templates actually used for in Power Automate?

options.text: As demos to learn how Power Automate flows work.
As working flows, which you can select and start using for business use.
As partially working flow templates, which need several design changes.
A template with actions only. You need to add conditions

explanation: Templates in Power Automate are pre-built, fully functional workflows designed to help users quickly implement common automation scenarios without having to build a flow from scratch. What Templates Offer: Ready-made structure: Includes the trigger and actions required for a specific task. Business relevance: Templates often reflect real-world business processes, such as: Sending email reminders Syncing files between systems Collecting form responses Creating approval flows Customizable: While they work out-of-the-box, you can modify them to suit your exact needs.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Once a flow has been exported, who is able to import it?

options.text: Only the user that exported the flow
Anyone that receives the zip file can import it

explanation: When a Power Automate flow is exported, it is packaged as a .zip file (either as a package or logic app template, depending on the export format). This exported file can then be shared with anyone. Import Requirements: Any user with appropriate permissions in the target environment (typically “Environment Maker” or similar roles) can import the flow using the import feature in Power Automate. They do not have to be the person who exported it. Roles like System Administrator or Customizer are not strictly required for importing unless there are organization-specific permission policies in place. What the Import Process Involves: Upload the .zip file in Power Automate under My Flows > Import. Provide necessary connections and references (e.g., Outlook, SharePoint, etc.). Assign the flow to the correct environment or services. Save and use the imported flow. This makes sharing and reusing flows across teams, departments, or even organizations easy and efficient.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: During a training workshop at Zenith Technologies, participants are building an Employee Onboarding app for HR. The facilitator asks: who can actually get access to the Power Apps and Power Automate default environment?

options.text: Only users who have been assigned a Power Apps or Power Automate license
Only users with administrative privileges in Power Apps or Power Automate
Only users who are part of a specific security group or team

explanation: The default environment in Power Apps and Power Automate is automatically created for every Microsoft 365 tenant and is accessible to all licensed users within that tenant by default. Key Points: No manual addition required: Users do not need to be added by environment or tenant administrators to access the default environment. Automatic provisioning: As soon as a user logs in and has the proper license (e.g., Power Apps, Power Automate, or Microsoft 365 with embedded capabilities), they can begin building apps or flows in the default environment. Common use case: The default environment is often used for personal or small-scale automations and apps, though organizations may prefer to create separate environments for development, testing, and production for better control.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: The company wants highly tailored user interfaces with precise control over layout and experience, plus the ability to pull in data from multiple sources and add custom functionality for specific business processes. Which solution would you recommend for building pixel-perfect, custom UIs with drag-and-drop design?
explanation: Custom UI Design: Canvas apps allow full control over the layout and design using a drag-and-drop interface. Flexible Components: Developers can add buttons, galleries, forms, and other controls to create tailored user experiences. Multiple Data Sources: Canvas apps can connect to over 200 data sources, including SharePoint, Excel, SQL Server, and Dataverse. No-Code/Low-Code: Built using Power Fx, a simple Excel-like formula language, making it accessible to non-developers. Responsive Design: Apps can be optimized for mobile, tablet, or desktop use, depending on business needs. Rapid Prototyping: Ideal for quickly building and testing app ideas without complex setup. Role-Based Access: Security roles and permissions can be configured to control who sees what. Reusable Logic: Business logic and formulas can be reused across screens and controls. Reference https://powerapps.microsoft.com/en-us/roadmap/

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: A company is building a Power Pages site and needs out-of-the-box portal types to meet these requirements: 1) collaboratively onboarding new suppliers and distributors; 2) publishing a blog post announcing new suppliers. Which portal types should they use for each?
explanation: 1. Collaboratively onboard new suppliers and distributors - Partner Portal The Partner Portal is designed for business-to-business (B2B) scenarios. It supports secure external collaboration with partners, distributors, and suppliers. Provides features like case management, onboarding workflows, document sharing, and access based on security roles.1 2. Publish a blog post announcing new suppliers - Community Portal The Community Portal is ideal for public engagement and content publishing, such as: Blog posts Forums Knowledge base It supports anonymous and authenticated users, and offers content-focused features. Why Others are wrong? Customer Self-Service Portal This portal is designed for customers, not business partners. It’s focused on support scenarios like ticket submission and knowledge base access, not collaboration or onboarding of partners like suppliers or distributors. Portal from Blank While this gives you complete flexibility, it requires you to build everything from scratch. It doesn’t come with prebuilt features for partner onboarding, you'd have to recreate all B2B functionality manually, which is inefficient when a Partner Portal already meets the need.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You're building a Power Automate flow and need to do a one-off calculation or reformat data, say, concatenating strings or converting a date format, without needing to reuse the value across multiple steps. Which action would you use?
explanation: Exam Tips: Understanding Join, Compose, Select, and Filter Array is important for the PL-900 exam because these actions are commonly used in Power Automate to manipulate and process data efficiently

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: A company uses Microsoft 365, Power Platform, and Dynamics 365, and hasn't assigned any specific permissions to licensed users, yet those users can still create and edit Power Apps canvas apps. Which environment are they actually working in?
explanation: Default Environment: In Power Platform, if users are able to create and edit Power Apps canvas apps without assigned specific permissions, they are most likely doing so in the Default environment. The Default environment is automatically created for each tenant and is where users have permission to create and edit apps if no other environment is explicitly set up or permissions are not specifically restricted. This environment typically allows for broader access for users to create and test apps, especially in cases where licensing and permissions haven't been customized. Key Characteristics of the Default Environment: Automatic Creation: It is created automatically when the first user in the tenant signs up for Power Apps or Power Automate. Access: All licensed users in the tenant are automatically assigned the Environment Maker role, allowing them to create apps, flows, and other resources. Storage Capacity: The default environment includes: 3 GB Dataverse Database Capacity 3 GB Dataverse File Capacity 1 GB Dataverse Log Capacity It is limited to 1 TB of total storage capacity. Non-Deletable: The default environment cannot be deleted, and manual backups are not allowed (system backups are continuous). Why the other environments are incorrect: Production: This environment is typically used for live, production-grade apps, and it is more tightly controlled in terms of permissions and security. Users would usually not have the same level of access here as in the Default environment. Sandbox: This environment is usually used for testing, development, or experimentation. Permissions for creating apps here would typically be managed and more restricted. References: Power Platform environments overview - Power Platform | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: If a flow needs to pause and get a response from a person before continuing, which Power Automate concept would you use?
explanation: Approvals in Power Automate are specifically designed to pause a flow until a person provides input. You can create an approval request (like “Approve” or “Reject”) and the flow waits for a response before continuing. It's perfect for processes like vacation requests, document reviews, purchase orders, or any step that needs a human decision mid-flow. Why others are wrong: Decisions: These are automated choices in logic flows, not based on user input. Loops: Used to repeat actions, not for collecting responses. Controls: Encompasses conditions and branching logic not interactive user approvals.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You're building a Power App for Sales, and it needs a button that emails a proposal to a customer when clicked. What type of flow meets this requirement?
explanation: Instant flow is the right choice when you want to trigger an action manually, such as by pressing a button in a Power App. Why others are incorrect: Automated: Runs automatically based on a trigger (like a new record), not suitable for manual button presses. Scheduled: Runs at defined times, not in response to user interaction. Desktop: Refers to flows created in Power Automate Desktop, used for robotic process automation (RPA), not button-triggered cloud actions. Business Process Flow: Used to guide users through a defined process or workflow, not for sending an email from a button. Reference https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/flow-types

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: You need to explain the Dataverse security model to your manager. Which of these statements correctly describe what the Dataverse security model actually offers? (Select all that apply)

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Can you take an existing template and customize it further to fit your own needs?
explanation: Templates are meant to be a starting point they come with prebuilt screens, forms, and basic functionality. Provide data permissions for Excel file only

Without the correct permissions, users may be able to open the app but not view or interact with Dataverse data.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Which of these statements accurately describe how Power Automate uses connectors? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Power Automate flow can use not more than three connectors
Power Automate shares connections with Power Apps
Power Automate uses only the connection‘s trigger for the flows
Power Automate flow uses standard and premium connectors
Power Automate uses only certified custom connectors for the flows

explanation: How Power Automate Works with Power Apps Power Automate can be triggered from Power Apps in two ways: A. Using Power Automate as an Action in Power Apps Users can trigger a Power Automate flow from a button click inside a Power App.This is done using the Power Automate function inside Power Apps.Example: A user submits a request in Power Apps, and Power Automate sends an email confirmation. B. Power Automate Triggered by Data Changes in Power Apps A Power Automate flow can be triggered when a record is added, modified, or deleted in Power Apps.Example: When a new customer is added in Power Apps, Power Automate updates a SharePoint list. Automating Form Submissions and Approvals Challenge: Manually managing approval requests in emails leads to delays and inefficiencies.Solution with Power Automate & Power Apps: Users submit a leave request via Power Apps. Power Automate sends an approval request to the manager via Outlook or Teams. Manager approves/rejects the request, and Power Automate updates the status in Power Apps. Impact: Speeds up approval processes, reducing manual intervention. Benefits of Integrating Power Automate with Power Apps Reduced Manual Work: Automates repetitive tasks like approvals, notifications, and data entry.Seamless Integration: Connects Power Apps with Dataverse, SharePoint, Outlook, SQL, and more.Improved User Experience: Enhances Power Apps functionality by adding automated actions.Time and Cost Savings: Minimizes errors, improves efficiency, and speeds up workflows.Scalability: Works for small businesses and enterprise-level solutions. References https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/add-manage-connections https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/connectors How Power Automate Works with Power Apps - Rishan Solutions

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A company uses Power Platform with two requirements: users must not be able to share customer data with other users, and users must not connect to data sources without explicit permission. Which TWO types of policies would meet these security requirements?
explanation: Environment-level policies: These allow you to control data access and sharing within specific environments (e.g., development, test, production). You can configure Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies at the environment level to block connectors that could expose sensitive data. Ideal for segregating workloads and applying tailored security settings per environment. Tenant-level policies: These apply across the entire organization and act as a broader security boundary. You can enforce global DLP policies to prevent unauthorized data sharing between connectors or services. Useful for governing access to data sources and ensuring compliance across all environments.

section: Describe features and capabilities of agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio
text: You want to extend your Copilot Studio chatbot with actions that call a Power Automate flow. Can this work if the flow lives in a different Dataverse environment than the chatbot?
explanation: You can use Power Automate flow for your chatbot actions ONLY if a flow and chatbot are in the same Dataverse Environment. When you create a chatbot in Copilot Studio, it runs within a specific Dataverse environment. To call a Power Automate flow from your chatbot (e.g., to perform an action like sending an email, updating a record, etc.), the flow must be in the same environment as the chatbot. Cross-environment execution is not supported for chatbot-triggered flows. Keep in mind: Chatbot environment scope: When you create a chatbot in Copilot Studio, it is tied to a specific Dataverse environment. Flow execution requirement: Power Automate flows can only be triggered by chatbot actions if they are created in the same Dataverse environment as the chatbot. Cross-environment limitation: Chatbots cannot call flows that reside in a different environment. Cross-environment execution is not supported for chatbot-triggered flows. Practical implication: If you want your chatbot to perform tasks like sending emails, updating records, or integrating with external systems, you must ensure the flow is built in the same environment where the chatbot resides. Reference https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/learn/modules/introduction-power-virtual-agents/3-power-virtual-agents-components

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Azman needs to check the capacity usage of a Dataverse environment and free up storage space if possible. Where in the Power Platform admin center would he do this?
explanation: To check and manage storage capacity in Dataverse, follow these steps in the Power Platform Admin Center: Go to the Power Platform Admin Center. Select the Environment you want to review. In the lefthand menu, choose Resources. Click on Capacity. Free up space by identifying unused tables, removing unnecessary records, or optimizing data storage settings. Why others are wrong: Database Capacity = Database storage is just one part of capacity management. The full breakdown is found under "Resources -> Capacity." Resources -> Capacity = While this is close, selecting the Environment first ensures you're viewing the correct details. Dataverse Storage = No direct section named "Dataverse Storage" exists in the Admin Center; instead, storage details are shown under Capacity.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: If you build a connector yourself rather than using a pre-made one, what's it called?

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: True or false: connectors in Power Platform are used only to connect to data sources, while Power Automate is used to connect to external services.

They let you connect to: Data sources (like SharePoint, SQL Server) External services (like Outlook, Twitter, Salesforce) If you use: Outlook connector → send emails SharePoint connector → save or read files Twitter connector → post a tweet SQL connector → get database records

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Nathaniel built an app in Power Apps for Teams, using Dataverse, and needs to roll it out to everyone in the organization without manually adding each person to the Teams group. How can he do this?

options.text: He could export the coding and import it to the Power Apps environment
He would have to upgrade Dataverse for Teams to Dataverse. This would allow the app to be shared with all users.
He would have to export the app from Teams and import it to PowerApps
He would have to recreate the app in the standard PowerApps screen.

explanation: Dataverse for Teams limits app access to members of the specific Microsoft Teams team where the app was created. To roll out the app organization-wide, Nathaniel needs the flexibility that comes with Dataverse (full version). Upgrading allows the app to be moved to a Power Platform environment, enabling broader sharing options and centralized governance. Why others are wrong: Exporting "coding": Power Apps doesn’t really work through raw code export/import. Apps are exported as packages, and this alone won’t resolve access limitations. Exporting to PowerApps and importing again: This doesn’t bypass Dataverse for Teams limitations unless part of the upgrade. Recreating the app: Not necessary, upgrading is a smoother and supported path.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Gerald wants to add an element to a Power App that lets users pick from a list, but since the list has many options, it also needs to be searchable. What element should he use?

As the user types, it dynamically filters the list making it faster to locate items without scrolling endlessly. You can configure it to support single or multiple selections, depending on Gerald’s needs. Exam Tips: Describe common controls - Training | Microsoft Learn Understand the common controls being used in the Power apps. Why others are wrong: Gallery: Used for displaying lists of records not for selection. Drop Down: Allows selection from a list but does not support search natively.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A company built a custom app and its components in a Development environment, and is now moving everything into Production for end users. Once imported into Production, what type of solution is this classified as?
explanation: Unmanaged Solution: Purpose: Used primarily in development environments. Editable: All components (tables, forms, views, flows, apps, etc.) are fully editable. Customization: You can add, remove, or modify components freely. Export Use Case: Typically exported when moving to another development or test environment where further changes are expected. Version Control: Ideal for iterative development and source control. Managed Solution: Purpose: Used for deploying to production or other locked-down environments. Read-Only: Components are not directly editable once imported. Protection: Prevents accidental changes to core business logic or app structure. Export Use Case: Should be exported when deploying to production or any environment where changes should be restricted. Upgrade Path: Supports versioning and patching, making it easier to maintain and update over time. Best Practices: Develop in Unmanaged: Build and test your solution in an unmanaged state during development. Deploy as Managed: When ready for production or staging, export the solution as managed to preserve integrity. Avoid Editing Managed Components: If changes are needed, make them in the original unmanaged solution and re-export.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Daniella built a model-driven app, but every form, view, and chart for an entity is showing up for users. She wants to simplify things and only show specific ones. How can she remove certain forms, views, or charts from appearing?

options.text: All created views, forms and charts remain in the app
In the App Designer / Modern App Designer, items can be added or removed from the app.
Views, Forms and Charts can be removed from the solution
Views, Forms and Charts can be turned off

explanation: Model-driven apps are built using the App Designer (also known as the Modern App Designer). Daniella can select which forms, views, and charts to include by configuring the site map and the associated entities/tables. This doesn’t remove them from the Dataverse or solution, it simply hides them from the user interface of that specific app.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Leandro built an app that's published and available through the Power Apps mobile app. The CEO wants it available on iOS and Android without requiring people to install the Power Apps app itself. Is that possible?

options.text: The app can be wrapped and deployed to company phones using Intune or other MDM tool.
The app would need submitted to the iOS and Android stores
It is not possible to achieve this
The app can be sideloaded on Android but not on iOS

explanation: This question is purely for knowledge purpose to know about the Power Apps application. Distributing Power Apps Outside of the Power Apps Mobile App: Power Apps apps are not standalone mobile apps by default, they require the Power Apps container app to run. However, organizations can “wrap” the app using the Power Apps component framework and tooling like the Power Apps mobile packaging tool. Once wrapped, the app behaves like a standalone mobile app and can be: Deployed to corporate devices via Microsoft Intune or other Mobile Device Management (MDM) tools. Controlled in terms of updates, access, and branding,  ideal for enterprise distribution. Why others are wrong: Submitting to iOS and Android stores: Not directly supported. Power Apps aren't native apps designed for public app stores. Sideloading on Android only: Technically possible for testing, but not scalable or secure for enterprise use. “It is not possible”: Inaccurate, Microsoft provides official guidance for wrapping and internal deployment.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A government agency wants citizens to be able to submit service requests through a public portal. The requests need to be stored securely and trigger a workflow that assigns them to regional teams based on location. Which combination of tools best supports this?

B. Power Pages, Power Automate, and Dataverse

Power Automate triggers workflows based on location logic. Power Apps is not needed unless internal apps are required. Copilot Studio is irrelevant unless chat is involved. Why the other options are incorrect: A. Power Apps, Microsoft Copilot Studio, and Dataverse Power Apps is great for internal apps, not public portals. Microsoft Copilot Studio is not required for this scenario. C. Power Automate, Power Apps, and Microsoft Copilot Studio Again, Power Apps is not suited for public portals. No mention of secure data storage (Dataverse is missing). D. Power Pages, Power Apps, and Microsoft Copilot Studio No workflow automation tool (Power Automate is missing). Microsoft Copilot Studio is more about AI-driven interactions, not a fit here.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A startup wants to integrate its custom CRM system with Power Platform to sync customer data into Dataverse, and the CRM uses a proprietary API. What's the most appropriate solution?

options.text: A. Use a standard connector in Power Automate
B. Build a custom connector in Power Automate

You can then use Power Automate to sync the data into Dataverse on a schedule or event-driven basis. Why the other options are incorrect: A. Use a standard connector in Power Automate The scenario says it’s a custom CRM with a proprietary API, so no standard connector exists. C. Use Power Apps to manually enter data Manual entry is inefficient, error-prone, and doesn’t scale especially when syncing data is the goal.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: A business analyst uses Copilot in Power Apps to build a data model for tracking employee onboarding, telling it: "Create a table called 'Onboarding Tracker' with columns for Employee Name, Start Date, Role, and Manager." section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A consulting firm wants an internal app for submitting client billing reports, which should validate entries, store them in Dataverse, and notify the finance team via Outlook. What's the most efficient solution?

Power Automate Can trigger workflows when a report is submitted (e.g., send a notification to the finance team via Outlook). section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A company wants to automate invoice processing by connecting Power Automate to its SAP system. What licensing consideration needs to be addressed before implementing this?

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A company uses Power Automate to process customer orders stored in a Microsoft List. For each order, the flow needs to check if the total exceeds ₹50,000, if so, send an approval request to a manager; otherwise, send a confirmation email to the customer. What Power Automate features are needed to build this logic?

options.text: A. Apply to each loop and condition control
B. Do until loop and parallel branch
C. Scope control and terminate action
D. Switch control and delay action

explanation: Correct answer: A. Apply to each loop and condition control Explanation: The “Apply to each” loop processes each order individually. The “Condition” control enables branching logic based on the order total. “Do until” is for repeated execution until a condition is met, not for evaluating values. “Scope” and “terminate” are used for error handling. “Switch” is for multiple discrete cases, and “delay” is for time-based actions.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A solution architect is designing a Dataverse model for a customer-relationship app and needs to link multiple contacts to multiple accounts. Which relationship type should they use?

text: An enterprise wants only finance-department users to be able to access a specific Power App that handles sensitive budget data. What governance feature would enforce this?

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A user wants to build a Power App that connects to Salesforce data. What licensing tier is needed to enable that?

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A solution architect wants to bundle multiple apps, flows, and tables into a single deployable unit for a client. Which Power Platform feature supports this?

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A business wants to embed a Power App directly into a Microsoft Teams channel so employees can access it easily. What integration capability enables this?
