section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Which of these are actual types of views supported in model-driven apps? (Select all that apply)
explanation: Before we explore how to create views, it's important to understand the different types of views that are available. Model-driven apps support three types of views, each serving distinct purposes: Personal views: Custom views created and owned by individual users within the system. Personal views are only visible to the user who created them unless explicitly shared with others. Users have full control over these views and can customize them to meet their specific needs. This includes filtering data, organizing information, or displaying specific fields. System views: These predefined views are part of the core functionality of the system. Examples of system views include Quick Find, which is used for rapid searches; Advanced Find, which enables complex queries (also used to create personal views); Associated Views, which display related records; and Lookup Views, used for selecting records in lookup fields. Unlike personal views, system views are managed at the administrative level, meaning only system administrators or customizers have the authority to modify them. Their design ensures consistency and reliability across the application, supporting essential operations and interactions. Public views: Public views are views that are accessible to all users within the application. These views can be customized to meet the specific needs of an organization. They're often used in subgrids, which display related records within forms, or dashboards, where they provide a summarized view of key data points. Create and modify views - Training | Microsoft Learn

explanation: Desktop flows and cloud flows serve distinct purposes, but together they offer a powerful way to automate tasks across different environments. Desktop flows are tailored for automating processes on your local machine, such as interacting with installed software, legacy applications, or performing repetitive tasks like data entry. On the other hand, cloud flows are designed to connect and automate tasks across cloud-based services and platforms, enabling seamless integration between tools like Outlook, SharePoint, Teams, and more. Think of Copilot controls act as intelligent assistants embedded within your app. They allow users to ask questions or perform actions using conversational language, making it easier to access insights and interact with data without needing complex navigation or manual input. C. Interacting with legacy applications by simulating clicks, typing, and navigation

E. Receiving daily information updates, such as weather or stock prices, without manual effort
F. Organizing client invoices and receipts efficiently for freelancers or small businesses

explanation: Here are some examples of desktop flow use cases: Organizing files automatically: Imagine you frequently download reports or images from emails and need to sort them into specific folders. With desktop flows, you can set up an automated process to move files into designated folders based on their names or file types. For instance, all PDF invoices could automatically be sorted into a folder named "Invoices," saving you time and effort. Extracting data from websites: Suppose you're tracking product prices or gathering information from a weather website. Desktop flows can automate web scraping tasks, pulling data from websites and storing it neatly in an Excel spreadsheet. This capability eliminates the need for manual copying and pasting, allowing you to focus on analyzing the data instead. Interacting with legacy applications: Many businesses still rely on older systems like terminal emulators or applications that require manual input via user interfaces. Desktop flows can simulate human actions, such as clicking buttons, entering text, or navigating menus, using UI elements, images, or even screen coordinates. For example, you could automate data entry into an outdated Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system that doesn't support modern APIs. Desktop flows are incredibly versatile and cater to a wide range of users. A weather enthusiast might want to automate the process of receiving daily updates from weather websites. An office employee reducing the time spent on repetitive data entry tasks in legacy systems. Or a freelancer organizing client invoices and receipts efficiently. By using desktop flows, you can simplify complex processes and reduce errors. Power Automate also has prebuilt templates you can use as a starting point and customize to meet your needs. section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You're building a Power Automate cloud flow that needs to reach data from a third-party application exposing a REST API, but no prebuilt connector exists for it. Which TWO approaches could you use? (Select all that apply)

explanation: For PL900 exam point of view, knowing the below is sufficient: Using the HTTP connector is a valid solution for accessing data in a third-party application with a REST API when there is no specific connector available is sufficient. Creating a custom connector is a valid solution for accessing data in a third-party application with a REST API when there is no pre-built connector available What is REST API? One system (called the client) sends a request to another system (called the server). The server processes the request and sends back a response, usually in a format like JSON. REST APIs use standard web methods like GET (to read data), POST (to create data), PUT (to update data), and DELETE (to remove data). These interactions happen over HTTP, the same protocol your browser uses to load websites. REST APIs are popular because they’re easy to use, scalable, and work well with many types of applications.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Contoso Ltd. wants to manage permissions efficiently across its Power Platform environment. What's the main purpose of Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)?

options.text: A) To assign usernames and passwords to all users
B) To define what actions users can perform and what data they can access
C) To encrypt all application data
D) To create backups of all user records

explanation: Role-based access control (RBAC) allows administrators to assign security roles to users that define what actions they can perform and what data they can access. For example, a "System Administrator" role might grant full control over all resources, while a "Basic User" role might allow viewing specific records but not making changes. RBAC operates at multiple levels: Environment-level access: Controls access to apps, flows, and resources within specific environments, such as development or production. App-level access: Restricts access to individual apps or components within an environment. Record-level access: Provides granular control over who can view, edit, or delete specific records. References: Describe the Power Platform security model - Training | Microsoft Learn

D) To allow administrators to bypass security protocols

explanation: Users can have multiple security roles assigned to them. This allows organizations to easily provide access to resources, apps, and records as needed. By following the principle of least privilege access, users only have the permissions they need, reducing risks from accidental or malicious actions. Administrators can easily assign and update roles as organizational needs evolve, balancing accessibility with protection.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You want to stop Dataverse from being able to connect to an email connector within Power Automate. What would you use to enforce that?
explanation: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) Policies in Power Platform, including Power Automate and Dataverse, are used to protect sensitive data by ensuring that it is not shared inappropriately between connectors that should not be communicating with each other. Purpose of DLP Policies: Prevent Unintended Data Sharing: DLP policies control which connectors can be used together within a flow or app. This prevents sensitive data from being sent from one service to another, like from a business-critical system to a personal or less secure service. Enforce Compliance: DLP policies ensure that data handling complies with organizational policies, industry regulations, and privacy laws. Why you need to know about DLP for PL900 exam: Security Awareness: PL-900 covers foundational knowledge, including how to build apps and automate workflows. Understanding DLP ensures you're aware of how to protect organizational data while doing so. Governance Best Practices: DLP is a key part of governance strategy. Knowing how it works helps you understand how organizations manage risk and maintain compliance when using Power Platform tools. Connector Control: DLP policies define which connectors (like SharePoint, Outlook, Twitter, etc.) can be used together. This is crucial when building apps or flows, as some combinations may be restricted. Real-World Scenarios: Many exam questions are based on practical use cases. You might be asked to identify the impact of a DLP policy or troubleshoot why a flow isn’t working due to connector restrictions. Admin vs. Maker Perspective: Even though PL-900 is a fundamentals exam, it introduces the roles of admins and makers. Makers need to understand how DLP policies affect their ability to build solutions. References: 8 Power Platform DLP Policy Best Practices

text: A project manager wants application changes tested before they reach production, following a consistent deployment process. Which capability supports this?
explanation: The correct answer is A. Power Platform Pipelines. Here is why: What it is: Power Platform Pipelines are tools that automate the movement of software solutions between different environments. How it helps: They handle deploying your apps from a Development environment to a Testing (UAT) environment, and finally to Production. Real-World Analogy: Think of a pipeline like a secure airport baggage conveyor belt. It takes your luggage (your app) from the check-in desk (development) through security and screening (testing), and safely to the final destination (production) following the exact same path every single time. Key Benefit: It ensures consistency and requires that an app is successfully moved and tested in lower environments before it can ever be released to real users. Here is why the other options do not fit your specific requirement: Security Roles: These determine who can see or do things in the app, not how the app itself is moved or tested. Topics: These are used in Copilot Studio to organize conversation flows for a chatbot. Business Rules: These are simple, no-code rules used to validate data entry on a form.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: While building a flow in the flow designer, you need to insert a missing step. What are the two options available for that new node?
explanation: In a flow designer (like Power Automate or similar workflow tools), when inserting a missing step, the two most relevant and common options you can choose from for the new node are: Add an action Add a condition Logical Order for Designing a Power Automate Flow 1. Trigger The trigger is what starts the flow. Every flow must have a trigger. Example: When a customer submits a support request form, the flow starts automatically. 2. Initialize Variables (Optional) Variables are used to store information that may be needed later in the flow. Example: Store a priority value such as "High" or a counter that tracks the number of items processed. 3. Get Data Retrieve any information needed before making decisions or performing actions. Example: Get customer details from Dataverse, retrieve an order from SharePoint, or look up employee information from Microsoft 365. 4. Apply Conditions Conditions allow the flow to make decisions based on data values. Example: Check whether a support ticket is marked as High Priority. If it is, send it for approval; otherwise, assign it directly to a support agent. 5. Apply Loops or Parallel Branches Loops Used when the same action must be repeated for multiple items. Example: Process each attachment in an email one at a time. Parallel Branches Used when multiple tasks can run at the same time. Example: Send an email notification and create a support ticket simultaneously. 6. Perform Actions Actions are the tasks that the flow performs. Examples: Send an email Create or update a record Post a Teams message Create a file Update a SharePoint item 7. Configure Approvals (If Needed) Approvals are used when someone must review and approve a request before the process continues. Example: A manager approves or rejects an employee leave request before the flow proceeds. 8. Compose or Parse Data (Optional) Compose Used to format or combine data. Example: Combine a first name and last name into a full name. Parse JSON Used to convert structured data into fields that can be used within the flow. Example: Extract customer details returned from an external system. 9. Error Handling or Scope Setup (Advanced) Error Handling Defines what happens if an action fails. Example: Send a notification to an administrator if a record cannot be created. Scopes Group related actions together for easier management and troubleshooting. 10. Terminate The final step that explicitly ends the flow and indicates its outcome. Example: End the flow with a status of Succeeded after all tasks complete successfully, or Failed if a critical error occurs. Reference https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/learn/modules/get-started-flows/2-create-first-flow https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/power-automate/parallel-modern-approvals

Relationships define connections between tables, enabling users to establish logical associations between different sets of data. Views display filtered data based on specified criteria, providing users with customized perspectives on their datasets. Fields represent individual data points within a table, allowing users to define the specific attributes and values associated with each record.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Which of these is actually true about Dataverse? A. It's a cloud storage service for files. B. It's a relational database for Power Platform. C. It's used to create chatbots. D. It's a data-visualization tool.
explanation: Microsoft Dataverse is a cloud-based data platformIt securely stores and manages data used by Power Platform apps, flows, and agents. Dataverse is required for solutionsSolutions are built on Dataverse and cannot exist without it. Dataverse uses tables, not databasesData is organized into tables (formerly called entities), with rows and columns. Standard and custom tables are supportedDataverse includes many standard tables (Account, Contact) and allows custom tables. Security is role-basedAccess to data is controlled using security roles, ensuring users see only what they are allowed to see. Dataverse integrates with Power Apps, Power Automate, and Copilot StudioAll Power Platform components can read and write Dataverse data. Business rules can be applied without codeYou can enforce logic such as field validation and default values. Dataverse supports relationships between tablesOne-to-many and many-to-many relationships are supported. Dataverse provides auditing and change trackingHelps with compliance and understanding data changes. Dataverse is environment-specificEach Power Platform environment has its own Dataverse instance.

section: Describe features and capabilities of agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio
text: A company wants an agent that can answer questions from company documents and create support tickets in an external system. Which TWO Copilot Studio capabilities are required for this?
explanation: Knowledge Sources allow your AI agent to read company documents, policy manuals, and websites to ground its answers. Tools are actions or workflows (such as Power Automate flows or APIs) that let your agent physically "do" things in external business systems, like opening a new support ticket in Jira, ServiceNow, or a CRM. Why others are wrong: C. Views is wrong: In the Microsoft ecosystem (like Power Apps or Dataverse), a "View" is simply a filtered grid or list used to display rows of data to a human user. An AI agent does not look at a visual list or layout grid to find answers; it uses search indexes to scan documents directly. D. Forms is wrong: A "Form" is a visual data-entry screen with blank fields (like Name, Email, and Description) designed for a human to type into. While Copilot can help a human fill out a form, an autonomous agent does not navigate a visual form to create a ticket. Instead, it extracts the necessary information directly from the conversation and pushes it to the external system using background code or APIs (Tools). E. Dashboards is wrong: A "Dashboard" is a visual collection of charts, graphs, and analytics used by managers to monitor performance trends (e.g., how many total tickets were opened this week). It is a reporting tool for humans, not a functional capability that helps an agent process natural language or execute background tasks.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Which of these statements about Dataverse are actually correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Dataverse includes standard tables such as Accounts and Contacts that can be used in business applications.
B. Dataverse supports custom tables, columns, relationships, and views to meet business requirements.
C. Dataverse only supports text and numeric data types.
D. Dataverse provides role-based, row-level, and field-level security.
E. Dataverse supports one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many relationships.
F. Dataverse cannot integrate with external systems such as SQL Server, SharePoint, or Excel.

explanation: 10 things to know about Dataverse: It’s a Scalable, Cloud-Based Data PlatformDataverse is Microsoft's secure, cloud-based platform for storing and managing data used by business applications. Works Seamlessly with Power PlatformIt integrates natively with Power Apps, Power Automate, Power Copilot Studio enabling low-code/no-code development. Standard Tables (Entities) Come Built-InDataverse includes a set of standard tables like Accounts, Contacts, and Products,  making it easier to build business apps quickly. Supports Custom Tables and FieldsYou can create your own tables (formerly "entities"), relationships, columns, and views to tailor the data model to your needs. Includes Rich Security ModelRole-based security, row-level security, and field-level security help control access to data at multiple granularities. Enables Business Logic Without CodeThrough business rules, workflows, and calculated/rollup columns, Dataverse lets you enforce logic and validation directly within the data layer. Data Types Are Rich and StructuredIt supports various data types , text, number, lookup (relationship), file, image, choice sets, and even complex types like customer and owner. Supports Relationships and Referential IntegrityDataverse supports 1-to-1, 1-to-many, and many-to-many relationships, just like a relational database. Solutions Enable App Lifecycle ManagementDataverse apps, flows, and components can be bundled into solutions for easy packaging, versioning, and deployment between environments. Integrates with External SystemsYou can bring data from SQL, SharePoint, Excel, Azure, and other systems using Dataflows, Connectors, or Power Query. Reference https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/learn/modules/introduction-common-data-service/2-overview

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: You've built a canvas app. What service would help you verify it's accessibility compliant?
explanation: App checker is a built-in tool in Power Apps that helps you identify issues related to: Accessibility Performance Formula errors Runtime issues It specifically flags accessibility violations (like missing labels or color contrast issues), which is essential for making your canvas app compliant with accessibility standards. Why others are wrong? Service Trust Portal = Provides info about Microsoft's security and compliance practices, not app-level accessibility checks. Compliance Manager = Helps manage organization-wide compliance (e.g., GDPR, ISO), not Power Apps-specific issues. Microsoft Trust Center = Offers transparency into Microsoft’s overall privacy and security practices, not app validation. 10 Key Points on App Checker (Power Apps): Built-in Tool for Canvas AppsApp Checker is integrated directly into Power Apps Studio, allowing real-time feedback as you build your canvas app. Checks for Four Main Categories of Issues Formula issues (e.g., syntax errors) Accessibility issues (e.g., missing labels) Performance warnings Runtime errors Helps Ensure Accessibility ComplianceApp Checker flags items like missing screen reader labels, poor color contrast etc. Provides Fix SuggestionsFor many issues, App Checker doesn’t just flag the problem,  it suggests how to fix it directly. Real-Time Issue DetectionAs you make changes to your app, App Checker updates in real time, so you can catch issues early in the development cycle. Prioritizes Issues by SeverityIt shows critical errors, warnings, and informational messages so developers can prioritize what needs fixing. Improves App PerformanceFlags inefficient formulas or nested controls that could slow down the app, guiding you toward better practices. Improves App Quality and MaintainabilityBy catching formula and logic issues, it helps prevent bugs that could affect users after deployment. Supports Deep Linking to IssuesClicking on an issue in App Checker takes you directly to the affected control or formula saving time. Essential for Publishing Production-Grade AppsUsing App Checker before publishing ensures your app meets Microsoft's standards for reliability, accessibility, and usability. References https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/powerapps/maker/canvas-apps/accessible-apps https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/powerapps/maker/canvas-apps/accessibility-checker Exam Tips: Understand how App checker in Power Apps and Flow Checker in Power Automate works for PL900 exam point of view. Recommended Youtube Video: App Checker in Power Apps - Must for All Developers Power Automate 101 | Flow checker tip

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Which of these are actual key features of environment security? (Select all that apply)
explanation: Key features of environment security include: Access control: Administrators decide who can access each environment and what actions they can perform. Data segmentation: Sensitive data is kept isolated, meeting compliance requirements like storing patient data separately in healthcare. Policy enforcement: Rules like Data loss prevention (DLP) policies ensure sensitive data stays protected. Lifecycle management: Environments support stages like development, testing, and production, so you can test safely before going live. Integration with Dataverse: Many environments use Microsoft Dataverse, adding extra security like row-level permissions to control data access. References: Describe the Power Platform security model - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: You're building a canvas app in Power Apps for your sales team that needs to pull customer info from SharePoint lists and update records in Dataverse. What would you use to set up and manage the data access between the app and these external sources?
explanation: Connectors allow you to connect to a variety of data sources, such as Microsoft 365, SQL Server, and more, to retrieve and manipulate data. Cloud service, Azure service, and datacenter are not appropriate for data access in canvas apps since they do not provide the necessary data retrieval and manipulation capabilities.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You're creating an automated flow from a template that needs to send an email whenever a new file is uploaded to the OneDrive Documents folder. What's the next step once your trigger is set up?
explanation: Power Automate Flow Basics: Every flow begins with a trigger (e.g., receiving an email in your inbox). After the trigger, you define one or more actions (e.g., sending an approval request or email). In the example flow, the action is to send an email after the trigger occurs. Important Limitations to Consider Adding Common Data Service (Dataverse) to a flow may prevent sending emails or uploading files to OneDrive. Email triggers or conditions in a flow can also block email sending or file uploads. If you're using a Business Process Flow and a file is uploaded to the OneDrive Documents directory, no email will be sent automatically. These limitations can affect how your flow behaves and should be considered during design. Choose action - Once the trigger is activated, you need to define the action the flow should take, such as sending an email notification. Why others are wrong? Add Common Data Service - Not necessary for this scenario, as you are working with OneDrive and email notifications, not Dataverse. Add a condition - Adding conditions is optional and only needed if you want to filter based on specific criteria, such as file type or folder location. Create Business Process Flow - Business Process Flows are used for structured workflows in Dataverse applications and not required for a Power Automate flow triggered by OneDrive. Reference https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/learn/modules/build-automated-solution/2-create-flow-template

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Match each environment type to its use case. Types: A. Production, B. Sandbox, C. Default, D. Trial. Use cases: hosting live applications; testing new features; general use; temporary testing.
explanation: Production environment (A) is used for hosting live applications, ensuring stability and reliability for end-users. Sandbox environment (B) is typically used for testing new features and changes before deploying them to the production environment. Default environment (C) is generally used for general day-to-day activities and development tasks. Trial environment (D) is a temporary environment used for testing out the platform's capabilities before making a decision to purchase or subscribe.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: In a business setting, who are valid target audiences for a Power Pages site? (Select all that apply)

B. Business partners participating in vendor or supplier processes
C. Employees using internal company portals and services

Organizations can provide self-service portals for support requests, order tracking, warranty management, and account management. B. Business partners participating in vendor or supplier processesPower Pages can be used for partner-facing scenarios such as vendor onboarding, dealer registration, supplier collaboration, and partner management. D. section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: Match each ALM stage to its description. Stages: a) Planning, b) Development, c) Testing, d) Deployment, e) Maintenance. Descriptions: monitor and update the application over time; define business requirements, goals, and scope; build the application using tools like Power Apps; validate the application in a testing environment; move the application to a production environment.
explanation: The stages of ALM: ALM in Power Platform can be broken down into several key stages: Planning: Define the business requirements, goals, and scope of the application. This stage involves gathering input from stakeholders and creating a roadmap for development. Development: Build the application using tools like Power Apps, Power Automate, and Dataverse. During this stage, developers collaborate to create and refine the app’s components. Testing: Validate the application in a testing environment to ensure it meets requirements and functions as expected. This stage helps identify and fix issues before deployment. Deployment: Move the application to a production environment, where it becomes available to end users. Solutions play a critical role in this stage by packaging all components and ensuring a smooth transition. Maintenance: Monitor and update the application over time to address bugs, add new features, and adapt to changing business needs. Exam Tips: Questions on Environment, DLP, ALM are sure to come. Do understand go through the learning path again and again. References: Describe Application lifecycle Management (ALM) in Power Platform - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Describe the business value of Microsoft Power Platform
text: True or false: managed solutions must be used to distribute a Power Platform application on AppSource.
explanation: When publishing to AppSource = Microsoft’s marketplace for business apps, your app has to be in a managed solution format. Why? Because AppSource installations go into external environments, and Microsoft requires apps to be packaged securely. Managed solutions ensure no unwanted edits or changes can happen after import, they’re like a sealed package ready for consumption. Key Point: For AppSource, unmanaged isn’t an option. It must be managed for controlled, professional deployment.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: What's the primary purpose of the Power Platform admin center?

options.text: A. To manage environments, security, governance, and resources across the Power Platform
B. To monitor application performance and usage analytics for individual apps
C. To create and manage Dataverse tables, relationships, and business rules

explanation: It is the main tool for managing all Power Platform components, including Power BI, Power Apps, Power Automate, and Copilot Studio. Administrators use it to create and manage environments for development, testing, and production. It allows control over settings, such as data policies, user roles, and permissions. It helps manage resources, including licenses, capacity, and connectors. It supports security and access control, ensuring users have the right permissions and data protection is in place. Let's check why other options are incorrect? A. To manage environments, security, governance, and resources across the Power PlatformThe Power Platform admin center is used by administrators to manage environments, users, security, capacity, data policies, and overall governance. B. To monitor application performance and usage analytics for individual appsWhile administrators can view analytics in various places, monitoring app performance is not the primary purpose of the Power Platform admin center. C. To create and manage Dataverse tables, relationships, and business rulesDataverse tables and business rules are typically managed within Power Apps and Dataverse tools, not the admin center's primary function. D. To configure connectors and establish connections to external data sourcesConnectors are configured when building apps and flows. The admin center may provide governance controls, but creating connections is not its primary purpose. These distractors are better for PL-900 because all four options sound Power Platform-related and require understanding the distinction between administration, development, data modeling, and connectivity. References: Module assessment - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Which of these correctly pairs a Power Automate flow type with its description? A. Instant flow, runs on a schedule. B. Scheduled flow, runs manually. C. Desktop flow, automates tasks on a computer. D. Business process flow, automates repetitive tasks.
explanation: Desktop flow - Automates tasks on a computer. Desktop flows are used for robotic process automation (RPA) to automate tasks on a computer. Instant flows run manually, scheduled flows run on a schedule. Business process flows guide users through processes.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Which Power Platform feature lets you connect a Power App to Outlook?
explanation: A. EnvironmentAn environment is a workspace that stores and manages Power Platform resources such as apps, flows, Dataverse tables, and users. It helps separate development, testing, and production resources, but it does not provide connectivity to Outlook. B. ConnectorA connector is used to establish a connection between Power Platform and external services or data sources. Microsoft Outlook has a built-in connector that allows Power Apps and Power Automate to send emails, manage calendars, and access Outlook data. This is the correct answer. There are two types of connectors: Prebuilt: Predefined connectors that can be used without you making modifications. They address automating commonly used business process scenarios. Custom: Function-based connectors that you build to support your tailored scenarios C. SolutionA solution is a container used to package and manage Power Platform components, such as apps, flows, tables, and customizations. Solutions help with application lifecycle management and deployment between environments, but they do not connect apps to Outlook. D. GatewayA gateway enables secure communication between Power Platform cloud services and on-premises data sources, such as local SQL Server databases or file shares. Outlook is a cloud service and does not require a gateway connection. References: Connectors overview | Microsoft Learn

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Match each Common Data Model (CDM) feature to its purpose. Features: A. Standard schema, B. Data integration, C. Relational data storage, D. Metadata management. Purposes: 1. Provides consistency across apps. 2. Enables data sharing. 3. Stores structured data. 4. Manages data definitions.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: True or false: managed solutions always protect Power Platform components from being edited once they're exported to another environment.
explanation: This is one of the strongest features of managed solutions: they lock the configuration of your app components. When exported/imported to another environment (say, from development to test or production), users cannot modify forms, workflows, or tables from the managed solution directly. This protects your intellectual property and prevents accidental changes that could disrupt functionality. Key Point: Once a component is part of a managed solution, it’s effectively read-only in the target environment.

explanation: Canvas apps allow users to design apps with a drag-and-drop interface and run them on browsers or mobile devices.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Match each licensing model to its feature. Models: A. Per-user plan, B. Per-app plan, C. Pay-as-you-go, D. Free plan. Features: unlimited app creation; access to specific apps; charges based on usage; no premium connectors.

options.text: A - 1 (Per user plan allows unlimited app creation)
B - 2 (Per app plan provides access to specific apps)
D - 4 (Free plan does not include premium connectors)
D - 2 (Per app plan provides access to specific apps)

explanation: The Per user plan in Microsoft Power Platform allows users to create an unlimited number of apps without any restrictions. This licensing model is suitable for organizations or individuals who need the flexibility to create multiple apps tailored to their specific needs. On the other hand, the Per app plan provides access to specific apps, limiting the user's access to only the designated applications. This model is ideal for users who require access to a limited set of applications based on their roles or responsibilities. Additionally, the Pay-as-you-go model charges users based on their actual usage of the platform, making it a cost-effective option for organizations with fluctuating usage patterns. Lastly, the Free plan does not include premium connectors, limiting the user's access to advanced integration capabilities that require premium features. A - 1 (Per user plan allows unlimited app creation) B - 2 (Per app plan provides access to specific apps) C - 3 (Pay-as-you-go charges based on usage) D - 4 (Free plan does not include premium connectors)

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Olivia built a flow that occasionally fails to complete and throws errors. What's one way to check its run history and see the errors?

options.text: She will not be able to check errors unless a notification step has been added
Select Failed Runs from the Run History window

explanation: How to Check Errors in Power Automate: Open Power Automate Go to "My Flows" and select the flow experiencing issues. Click on "Run History" to view past executions. Select a failed run to inspect the error messages and debugging details. References: Troubleshoot a cloud flow - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A flow connects to Excel and sends staff reminder notifications, but the date shows up in the wrong format. What should be used in the flow to fix this?
explanation: To correctly format the date in Power Automate notifications, an Expression should be used within the flow. The formatDateTime() function allows users to define the preferred date format before sending the notification. Why others are wrong? Use a Condition = Conditions are used to evaluate logical statements but do not modify date formatting. Use the Date Time Connector = No specific "Date Time Connector" exists; instead, expressions within Power Automate handle date formatting. Format the date in Excel = Formatting in Excel does not guarantee the correct format when the data is retrieved in Power Automate, as it may still appear in the default system format. References: Customize or format date and time values in a flow - Power Automate | Microsoft Learn

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment

explanation: Power Platform allows you to build apps, flows, dashboards, etc., and solutions act as containers to organize these components. During development, you can use unmanaged or managed solutions, but managed solutions help define clear boundaries and versioning. They’re ideal when collaborating across teams or preparing for deployment, especially when you want to lock components for integrity. Key Point: Managed solutions are helpful even during development if you're prepping for production or distribution.

text: What's the correct way to test a cloud flow in Power Automate?

C) Exporting and re-importing is used for migration, not testing. D) Sharing the flow does not guarantee a test run or provide controlled testing conditions.

text: What's the purpose of loops and branching in cloud flows?

section: Describe features and capabilities of agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio
text: How does Power Platform actually work together with Microsoft 365 apps and services, including Teams? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A) Power Apps can be embedded in Microsoft Teams and SharePoint
B) Power Automate can send notifications and schedule meetings in Outlook
C) Copilot Studio bots can be deployed directly into Microsoft Teams
D) Power Platform tools cannot interact with Microsoft 365 services

explanation: Microsoft Power Platform business solutions integrate seamlessly with Microsoft 365 apps and services to enhance productivity, automate workflows, and enable data-driven decision-making across familiar tools like Outlook, Excel, SharePoint, and Microsoft Teams. Here's how they work together: 1. Power Apps + Microsoft 365 Embed in Teams or SharePoint: Custom apps built with Power Apps can be embedded directly into Microsoft Teams tabs or SharePoint pages for easy access. Use Microsoft 365 connectors: Power Apps can connect to Excel, Outlook, and OneDrive to read or write data. Streamline tasks: Employees can submit forms, update records, or trigger actions without leaving Microsoft 365. 2. Power Automate + Microsoft 365 Automate emails and calendar events: Create flows that send Outlook emails or schedule meetings based on triggers. Manage SharePoint content: Automatically move, tag, or update documents and list items. Integrate with Teams: Send notifications, start approvals, or post messages in Teams channels based on business events. 3. Power BI + Microsoft 365 Embed dashboards: Power BI reports can be embedded in Teams, SharePoint, or Excel for real-time insights. Collaborate on data: Teams users can discuss and share Power BI visuals directly in chats or meetings. Excel integration: Analyze Power BI datasets in Excel using pivot tables and formulas. 4. Copilot Studio + Microsoft Teams Build chatbots for Teams: Use Copilot Studio to create bots that answer FAQs, route requests, or assist with HR and IT tasks. No-code interface: Bots can be built and deployed without coding, making it accessible to business users. Enhance internal support: Bots can escalate issues, collect feedback, or guide users through processes all within Teams. 5. Unified Experience Single sign-on and security: All tools use Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) for secure access and identity management. Data consistency: Dataverse ensures consistent data across apps, flows, and reports. Collaboration-first: Integration with Teams and Outlook ensures users stay productive in their daily workflows.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: Which TWO features should a company use to help ensure GDPR compliance in customer-facing applications?

options.text: A. Prompt users for consent before collecting or processing their personal data and record when consent was provided.
B. Allow users to request access to, correction of, or deletion of their personal data.
C. Share customer data with third-party partners by default to improve user experience.
D. Retain all customer data indefinitely to support future analytics.
E. Require users to create public profiles so their information is visible to other customers.

explanation: For the PL-900 exam, you do not need deep legal knowledge of GDPR. Focus on the key principles and how Microsoft Power Platform supports them. GDPR Basics to Remember 1. Consent Users should be informed about how their data will be used. Obtain consent when required. Keep records of consent. Exam clue: If an option mentions obtaining and tracking consent, it is often a good GDPR-related answer. 2. Personal Data Protection Personal data includes names, email addresses, phone numbers, IDs, location data, and other information that can identify a person. Protect personal data from unauthorized access. Exam clue: Security controls, role-based access, and data protection features generally support GDPR compliance. 3. Data Subject Rights Individuals have rights to: Access their data Correct inaccurate data Delete data ("right to be forgotten") Export their data in a portable format Exam clue: Features that allow users to view, update, or delete their personal data are GDPR-friendly. 4. Data Minimization Collect only the data that is necessary. Do not collect extra information "just in case." Exam clue: Answers that reduce unnecessary data collection are usually preferred. 5. Retention and Deletion Do not keep personal data longer than necessary. Implement retention and deletion policies. Exam clue: "Store data indefinitely" is usually a wrong answer. 6. Security and Access Control Limit access to personal data. Use authentication and authorization. Audit access where possible. Exam clue: Role-based security and auditing are often associated with compliance. 7. Privacy by Design Consider privacy requirements when designing applications. Protect data from the start rather than adding controls later. Exam clue: Features that proactively protect user data are usually preferred.

text: Employees at a company use Power Automate for personal productivity, and often overwrite their flows while editing definitions, with no way to undo changes after saving. Which TWO options would let them preserve or revert a flow to its current state?
explanation: The two correct options are: a) Export Exporting a flow creates a package (.zip) that can be imported later. This acts as a backup, so users can restore the flow to its previous state if needed. c) Save As Creates a copy of the existing flow under a new name. This allows users to keep the original intact while experimenting with changes in the duplicate. Why Not the Others b) Rename → Only changes the name of the flow; does not preserve or revert its state. d) Share → Grants access to other users but does not create a backup or version to revert to.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: Which of these are recommended best practices when using Record with Copilot to build desktop flows? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Plan your process by outlining the steps before recording

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You're enhancing a flow with Copilot and want to add an SMS notification at the end of the process. Which of these commands would achieve that?

explanation: Correct Answer: "Insert SMS notification after the last action." Why correct: This command is explicit about placement (after the last action) and type (SMS). Why others are wrong: End with sending an SMS → Less precise; Copilot may misinterpret placement. Notify via SMS → Too vague; doesn’t specify when or where in the flow. Best practice for Copilot prompts: Be specific about the action: “Add SMS notification using Twilio.” Be precise about placement: “Insert after the last action.”

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: You want to keep an eye on how well your flows are performing and spot patterns in errors or slowdowns. Which Power Automate feature gives you detailed insight into flow performance and error patterns?
explanation: The easiest way to analyze your flows is to use the built-in analytics. These analytics provide a centralized view of your flow’s performance, usage, and error patterns. These insights are accessible from the flow details page and are designed to help makers and administrators understand how flows are running and where potential issues may arise. There are three main sections available: Flow usage: The usage metrics display the number of actions executed by your cloud flows over time. For example, if a flow is triggered frequently but performs unnecessary actions, this data can help you identify opportunities to streamline the process and reduce resource consumption. Error analysis: Error analysis provides detailed information about the types of errors encountered, their frequency, and the last time they occurred. For instance, if a flow consistently fails due to a missing connection or invalid input, the error analysis tab highlights these issues, allowing you to address them promptly. Execution history: The execution history tracks your flow runs over the past 30 days, offering a timeline of successes and failures. This feature is useful for identifying trends, such as recurring failures during specific times or under certain conditions, which can inform troubleshooting efforts. Run and monitor a cloud flow - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A company has separate teams working on development and production. An admin wants to make sure applications being tested don't affect live business operations. What should the admin create?
explanation: Correct Answer: B. A new environment Why Correct Environments provide isolation between resources, data, apps, and flows. Creating separate environments for development and production is a common practice. Creating separate environments for development, testing, and production is a best practice. This separation ensures that changes made in development don’t immediately affect production users, and governance/security can be applied differently per environment. Example: Developers build and test a new app in the Dev environment, then move it to Prod once it’s stable. Why Others Are Wrong: Connectors Provide access to external or internal data sources (like SharePoint, SQL, Outlook). They do not isolate workloads or environments, they simply connect apps to data. Solutions Package components (apps, flows, tables, rules) for deployment across environments. They are a transport mechanism, not a way to isolate workloads. Gateways Connect Power Platform apps to on-premises data sources securely. They enable hybrid connectivity but do not provide environment-level isolation.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A department manager built a cloud flow, and another employee needs to be able to maintain it and update its configuration whenever the manager is unavailable. What should be done? A. Add the employee as a co-owner of the flow. B. Export the flow as a package. C. Create a new environment. D. Publish the flow again.

options.text: A. Add the employee as a co-owner of the flow
B. Export the flow as a package

explanation: Why Correct Co-owners can edit, manage, and maintain the flow. Co-owners have full management rights over a flow: they can edit, update connections, add/remove triggers or actions, and maintain it. They cannot delete the flow - only the original owner has that authority. This ensures shared responsibility for maintenance without risking accidental deletion. Example: A team of HR managers co-own a leave approval flow so they can update rules, but only the creator can delete it. Why Others Are Wrong: Exporting Packages a flow for deployment elsewhere. Does not grant management or ownership rights. New Environment Creates a separate workspace. Unrelated to flow ownership or maintenance. Publishing Makes a flow available for use. Affects availability, not ownership or management rights.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A sales rep should only be able to see the customer records assigned to them, not records assigned to other reps. Which feature best addresses this? A. Business Rules. B. Row-level security. C. Dataflows. D. Choice columns.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. Row-level security Why Correct Row-level security controls access to specific records. Row-level security (RLS) is used to control access to individual records in Dataverse or other data sources. It ensures that users only see the records they are authorized to view, based on their role or security configuration. Example: A salesperson may only see their own customer accounts, while a manager can see all accounts in their region. This is critical for data privacy, compliance, and organizational control. Why Others Are Wrong: Business rules Enforce logic at the data level (e.g., auto-populating fields, validation). They do not restrict access to specific records. Dataflows Handle data import and transformation into Dataverse or other sources. They are about moving and shaping data, not controlling who can see which records. Choice columns Store predefined values (like dropdown options). They help standardize data entry but do not provide security or access control.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: An organization wants suppliers to submit information through a website and check the status of their submissions, without ever touching internal systems. Which Power Platform product fits best? A. Power BI. B. Power Pages. C. Power Automate. D. Dataverse.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. Power Pages Why Correct Power Pages is designed for external-facing websites. Power Pages is the Power Platform capability for building external-facing websites. It allows organizations to create secure, data-integrated portals for customers, partners, or communities. Example: A company might build a customer support portal where users can log cases and track progress. It’s specifically designed for public or partner access, unlike apps that are internal-facing. Why Others Are Wrong: Power BI Focused on analytics and visualization. It helps users create dashboards and reports, not websites. Power Automate Automates workflows and processes behind the scenes. It cannot build or host websites. Dataverse Serves as the data storage and management layer for Power Platform. It provides structured data tables but does not create websites.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Apps
text: An employee wants to build a mobile app that lets warehouse staff update inventory counts through a touch-friendly interface. Which type of app should they build? A. Model-driven app. B. Canvas app. C. Power Pages site. D. Dataflow.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. Canvas app Why Correct Canvas apps provide full control over the user interface and are ideal for mobile experiences. Canvas apps give makers full control over the user interface (UI). You can drag and drop controls, design layouts freely, and connect to multiple data sources. They are especially suited for mobile and tablet experiences, where flexibility in design is critical. Example: A field service app where technicians can log work orders, capture photos, and sync data with Dataverse. Why Others Are Wrong: Model-driven apps These are data-driven and automatically generate UI based on Dataverse tables. They provide consistency but are less customizable in terms of design. Best for complex business processes, not for highly tailored mobile experiences. Power Pages Used to build external-facing websites. They are not apps for mobile or internal UI customization. Dataflows Handle data import and transformation into Dataverse or other sources. They are about backend data management, not user-facing app design.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A company needs to move an application, its related flows, and tables from a testing environment into production. What should be used to do this? A. Connection references. B. Solutions. C. Business rules. D. AI Builder.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. Solutions Why Correct Solutions package Power Platform components for deployment. Solutions are the packaging mechanism in the Power Platform. They allow you to bundle components like apps, flows, tables, business rules, and more into a single unit. This makes it possible to deploy, move, and manage functionality across environments (e.g., from development → test → production). Example: A solution might contain a model-driven app, its associated Dataverse tables, and automation flows, all deployed together. Why Others Are Wrong: Connection References Manage connections to external services (like SharePoint, SQL, Outlook). They ensure flows and apps can reuse connections consistently. They do not package components for deployment. Business Rules Enforce logic at the data level (e.g., auto-populating fields, validation). They are part of a solution but not the packaging mechanism itself. AI Builder Provides AI capabilities like form processing, prediction models, and object detection. It enhances apps with intelligence but does not handle deployment packaging.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A maker updates an application and confirms the latest version has been saved, but users say they can't see the new functionality. What's the most likely reason? A. The environment hasn't been refreshed. B. The application hasn't been published. C. The connector has expired. D. The solution hasn't been exported.

options.text: A. The environment has not been refreshed
B. The application has not been published
D. The solution has not been exported

explanation: Correct Answer: B. The application has not been published Why Correct Saving stores changes; publishing makes them available to users. In Power Apps, saving an app stores your changes in the editor. Publishing makes those changes available to end users. If you only save but don’t publish, users will continue to see the older version of the app. This distinction ensures developers can test and refine before releasing updates to production. Why Others Are Wrong: Environment Refresh Refreshing an environment updates metadata or syncs components. It does not control whether users see the latest app changes. Connector Issues Connector problems typically cause runtime errors (e.g., data not loading). They don’t prevent users from seeing updated app versions. Exporting Solutions Solutions are used for packaging and moving apps between environments. Exporting is not required for users in the same environment to see updates. Publishing alone is sufficient for visibility.

section: Manage the Microsoft Power Platform environment
text: A company lets employees use both business systems and personal cloud storage. IT wants to stop business data from automatically flowing into personal services through Power Platform automations. What should be implemented? A. Managed Environments. B. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies. C. Security Roles. D. Solutions.
explanation: Correct Answer: B. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies Why Correct DLP policies control which connectors can be used together, helping prevent business data from flowing to unauthorized services. DLP policies are designed to control which connectors can be used together in Power Platform apps and flows. They prevent sensitive business data from being inadvertently sent to unauthorized or consumer services. Example: A DLP policy might allow SharePoint and Dataverse connectors in the same app but block mixing them with Twitter or Dropbox. This ensures data governance and compliance across the organization. Why Others Are Wrong: Managed Environments Provide governance features like monitoring, limits, and analytics. They do not specifically prevent connector mixing, that’s the role of DLP policies. Security Roles Control user access to apps, tables, and records. They don’t govern how data flows between connectors or services. Solutions Package and deploy app components (tables, flows, apps) across environments. They are about deployment and lifecycle management, not data movement restrictions.

section: Demonstrate the capabilities of Power Automate
text: A company wants every sales rep to follow the exact same sequence of steps when qualifying opportunities, no matter who's entering the data. Which feature best meets this? A. Business Process Flow. B. Business Rule. C. Power Automate Flow. D. Dataflow.
explanation: Correct Answer: A. Business Process Flow Why Correct Business Process Flows guide users through predefined stages and steps in a process. Business Process Flows (BPFs) are designed to guide users step-by-step through a structured process. They define stages (major milestones) and steps (specific actions or fields to complete). Example: In a sales app, a BPF might guide a salesperson through stages like Lead Qualification → Opportunity → Proposal → Closing. This ensures consistency, compliance, and clarity across the organization. Why Others Are Wrong: Business Rules Purpose: Automate field behavior (e.g., show/hide, set default values, enforce validation). Limitation: They don’t provide a guided stage-by-stage process. Example: A rule might automatically set “Priority = High” if “Revenue > $1M,” but it won’t walk the user through a workflow. Power Automate Purpose: Automates workflows behind the scenes (e.g., send an email when a record is created). Limitation: It’s not user-facing guidance; users don’t see or follow it step-by-step. Example: A flow might notify a manager when a case is escalated, but it doesn’t guide the agent through case resolution. Dataflows Purpose: Import, transform, and load data into Dataverse or other sources. Limitation: They’re about data integration, not guiding users through business processes. Example: A dataflow might pull customer records from SQL into Dataverse, but it doesn’t help a salesperson move through a sales pipeline.

text: A development team is preparing to deploy an application from testing into production. Which feature should be used? A. Connection References. B. Security Roles. C. Business Rules. D. Dataflows.
